recipes.title: Piping Buttercream Frosting

items: Beat the butter 2 minutes, until light, fluffy, and pale.
On low speed, gradually add the powdered sugar, then the cream, vanilla, and salt.
Once combined, beat on medium-high 3–5 minutes. Scrape down the bowl and beat a couple of minutes more.

tips: Stiff enough for tall, piped swirls on cupcakes.
notes: Kindra recommended this one when Mom wanted to make cupcakes with big piped frosting.

items: 2 cups fresh snow peas or sugar snap peas
1/4 cup diced onion or green onions

ingredients.heading: Sauce
items: 1 Tbsp low-sodium soy sauce (or liquid aminos)
Stir the sauce ingredients together in a bowl and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and warm the chicken through. Set it aside.
Add the carrots to the skillet, cover, and cook 3 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Add the pea pods, onion, zucchini, and ginger and stir-fry 3–4 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Stir the sauce again and pour it in with the chicken. Cook, stirring, until thickened and heated through.
Sprinkle with peanuts if you like, and serve over rice.
Preheat the oven to 325°F. Grease and flour 2 small loaf pans, or line them with sprayed parchment.
Cream the butter and sugar. Beat in the eggs and bananas.
Mix in the flour, baking soda, and salt, then the vanilla.
Gently fold in the sour cream.
Divide between the pans and bake about 65 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.

recipes.title: Evelyn's Easy Chocolate Chip Cookies

items: Cream the butter and both sugars. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Mix in the flour, salt, baking soda, and baking powder.
Drop onto baking sheets and bake about 12 minutes, just until the edges start to brown.

notes: Evelyn (Thackeray)'s recipe, shared by Blake and Kindra.

recipes.title: Easy Chicken and Rice Casserole

items: 1 (10.5 oz) can unsalted cream of chicken soup
1 (10.5 oz) can unsalted cream of mushroom soup
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Spray a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Whisk the soups, broth, rice, and onion soup mix right in the dish (or in a bowl, then pour into the dish).
Stir in the broccoli, if using, and lay the chicken on top.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 1/2 hours, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through.

tips: Dad uses just 2 chicken breasts, cut into chunks.
notes: Mix it all in the baking dish and pop it in the oven. One of Dad's super-easy dinners.

recipes.title: Best Bran Muffins

items: 1 cup grated carrots (small or medium holes)
Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line a muffin tin with paper liners or spray it.
Soak the raisins in hot water 10 minutes to plump them, then drain.
Crush the Bran Flakes (you'll have about 1 1/2 cups). Stir them into the buttermilk and let stand 5 minutes.
Grate the carrots and chop the pecans.
In a mixing bowl, stir together the eggs, oil, brown sugar, and vanilla. Stir in the bran mixture, then the carrots, pecans, and raisins.
Whisk the flour, salt, baking powder, and baking soda and stir in just until combined. Don't overmix.
Fill the muffin cups to the top and bake about 25 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool a few minutes in the pan, then on a rack.

notes: Dad's favorite bran muffins.

recipes.title: Whitney's White Chicken Chili

items: 3 (15 oz) cans Great Northern or cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
2 jalapeños, finely chopped, membranes and seeds removed
1/2 cup sour cream or plain Greek yogurt
Blend 1 cup of the beans with 1/2 cup of the broth until smooth. Set aside.
In a large pot, melt the butter with the olive oil. Sauté the onion and jalapeños 2–3 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add the bean purée, the remaining broth, the water, the remaining beans, the green chiles, corn, lime juice, and all the spices.
Bring to a boil, then simmer 15–30 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the sour cream and chicken.

tips: **Milder version:** Mom skips the jalapeños and cayenne and uses just one small can of green chiles. She also uses a whole can of corn.
notes: Whitney's recipe.

recipes.title: Kindra's Chicken Pot Pie

items: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts (or 2–3 cups cooked and chopped)
1–2 whole carrots, peeled and diced small
1 medium yellow onion, peeled and diced small
2 tsp kosher salt, more or less to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper, more or less to taste
If the chicken is raw, cook and chop it.
Melt about 3 Tbsp of the butter in a large Dutch oven. Add the carrots and cook 5 minutes.
Add the onion and celery with 1 tsp of the salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Cook until the onion is soft and translucent and the carrots are tender but not mushy.
Add the rest of the butter. Once melted, stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, stirring often.
Pour in the warm broth and milk. Simmer, stirring occasionally, 5–8 minutes, until thickened.
Stir in the peas, corn, chicken, parsley, and thyme. Taste and add up to 1 tsp more salt and a little more pepper.
Preheat the oven to 375°F. Set ramekins on a rimmed baking sheet and divide the potatoes among them.
Spoon the filling over the potatoes, filling each to the brim. Let cool a bit.
Top with pie crust, crimp the edges, and cut a few slits in each.
Bake 20–25 minutes, until the crust is golden. Cool 10 minutes before serving.

tips: **Kindra's way:** skip the ramekins and serve the filling like a soup, with squares of prebaked pie crust on the side. Everyone adds as much crust as they want, and it stays crunchy.
notes: Mom had this at Kindra's and says it's amazing.

recipes.title: Elsie's Smoky Beans

items: 1 can butter beans or lima beans, drained
Brown the ground beef with the onion and drain.
Put everything in a slow cooker and stir well.

notes: Mom first had these at Grandma Elsie's. The family used to make them for General Conference weekend. The bacon and smoky flavor make it.

recipes.title: Chicken Ratatouille

items: 1 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces
Heat 1 Tbsp of the oil in a large pan. Add the chicken, season with the salt and pepper, and cook until no longer pink.
Sprinkle with 1 tsp of the Italian seasoning and cook 2 minutes more. Move to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the pan and sauté the garlic, onion, and green pepper until the onion is nearly translucent.
Add the zucchini and the remaining 1/2 tsp Italian seasoning. Cook until tender.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and the chicken. Simmer 5–10 minutes, then season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with parsley.
Serve with rice, mashed potatoes, pasta, or cauliflower rice.

tips: If the tomatoes taste too acidic, stir in about 1 tsp sugar.

recipes.title: Thai Coconut Soup (Tom Kha)

items: 1/2 yellow onion, or 1 bunch scallions, thinly sliced
1 1/2-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and minced
2 tsp lemongrass paste, or 1 stalk lemongrass (trimmed, peeled, and halved lengthwise)
Minced red bell pepper, for garnish (optional)
Extra vegetables, such as celery, carrots, peas, potatoes, or mushrooms (optional)
In a soup pot, combine the stock, onion, ginger, lemongrass, and jalapeños. Simmer over medium-low about 15 minutes. Add any extra vegetables now so they get tender.
Stir in the coconut milk, chili paste, curry paste, brown sugar, fish sauce, and chicken. Simmer 5 minutes more.
Stir in the lime juice and cilantro and season with salt. Remove the lemongrass stalk.

tips: The fish sauce adds a seafood note. Leave it out if you prefer.
notes: Dad's recipe.

recipes.title: Maple Brown Sugar Cinnamon Roll Frosting

items: Melt the butter and brown sugar in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Let cool slightly, then stir in the milk.
With a mixer, beat in the vanilla, maple flavoring, and powdered sugar until smooth.

notes: Mom first had this on cinnamon rolls while teaching at Waverly High School. She cut the recipe to a quarter, enough for one family-size pan of rolls.

recipes.title: Smash Burgers

items: Peanut oil or other neutral oil
American cheese, thinly sliced (fresh from the deli is best)
You'll need a cast iron skillet or flat-top griddle, a sturdy metal spatula, and a #12 scoop (or #16 for sliders).
Toast the buns in the hot skillet and set aside.
Heat the skillet over medium and spread a drop or two of oil over the surface.
Scoop heaping balls of beef onto the skillet, leaving about 3 inches around each. Cook just 2–3 at a time.
Salt each ball generously, then press it down **hard** with the spatula until it's a thin patty a little wider than the bun.
Leave them alone to cook about 2 1/2 minutes, until reddish juices appear on top.
Flip once (don't press again), top with cheese, and cook about 2 minutes more.

tips: Sliders cook a little faster. Flip when you see red juice on top.
Try one before adding condiments. They're great plain.

recipes.title: Applesauce Cookies

items: 1 package semisweet chocolate chips (mini chips work great)
Preheat the oven to 400°F and grease a cookie sheet.
Stir the baking soda into the applesauce.
Beat the sugars, shortening, and eggs, then mix in the applesauce.
Sift the flour, spices, and salt and add to the batter. Stir in the chocolate chips and nuts.
Drop by spoonfuls onto the cookie sheet and bake 9–12 minutes. They stay soft.

notes: A family recipe from Dad and NaTel Thackeray.

recipes.title: Jon's Apple Cake with Caramel Sauce

ingredients.heading: Cake
items: 3 cups peeled, chopped apples (1 tart and 2 sweet)
Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and spices.
In another bowl, whisk the oil, sugars, applesauce, eggs, vanilla, and orange juice. Stir into the dry ingredients, then fold in the apples.
Bake 45–50 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Tent with foil at the 30-minute mark so the top doesn't overbrown.

**Caramel sauce:** in a saucepan over medium heat, stir the butter, brown sugar, and cream constantly until it comes to a rapid boil. Boil 1 minute, then turn to low and simmer 1 minute more. Remove from the heat, stir in the powdered sugar, and let thicken about 20 minutes.
Serve the cake with caramel sauce drizzled over the top.

tips: If the sauce gets too thick, warm it briefly in the microwave.

recipes.title: Thackeray Reunion Granola

items: 2 cups chopped pecans or sliced almonds
In a large bowl, mix the oats, nuts, coconut, and brown sugar.
Stir together the coconut oil, maple syrup, salt, and vanilla and pour over the oats. Mix until coated.
Spread on 2 large baking sheets and bake 15 minutes.
Turn the oven off and leave the granola inside to finish toasting. Let cool.
Break into pieces for cereal or toppings.

notes: Made for the Thackeray family reunion, with Michelle.

recipes.title: Sausage, Egg, and Hash Brown Breakfast Casserole

items: 8 frozen hash brown patties (or a layer of tater tots)
Diced peppers, onions, or other veggies (optional)
Spray a 9x13-inch pan and lay the hash brown patties in the bottom.
Brown the sausage and sprinkle it over the potatoes, along with any vegetables.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt, and pepper and pour over the top. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake covered with foil 25 minutes, then uncover and bake about 20 minutes more, until set.

tips: Assemble the night before and refrigerate, covered, until you're ready to bake.

items: In a saucepan, heat the chicken and soup with enough milk to make a gravy. Add more milk as needed.
Set out the toppings in bowls.
Everyone builds their own: rice, then chicken gravy, then toppings.

recipes.title: Microwave Rice Krispie Treats

items: Butter a 9x13-inch dish. You'll need a large microwave-safe bowl.
Put the butter, cut into chunks, and 2 bags of marshmallows in the bowl. Microwave 1 minute and stir. Repeat until melted.
Stir in the third bag of marshmallows and microwave 30 seconds more. Stir; a few unmelted bits make them even better.
Stir in the cereal until coated and press into the dish.

tips: **Peanut butter version:** add 1 cup peanut butter with the butter and first 2 bags of marshmallows.
notes: Julie's recipe. The extra marshmallows make these extra gooey.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Thai Chicken Curry

items: 1 lb chicken breasts or thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
1 large bunch kale or spinach, cut into small pieces
Put everything except the coconut milk and kale in the slow cooker.
Stir in the coconut milk and kale and cook until the greens wilt. Thicken with a little flour if needed.
Serve over rice with lime wedges and cilantro.

tips: Add chopped chili peppers for more heat.

recipes.title: Silver Dollar City Ginger Cookies

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F and line a cookie sheet with parchment.
Cream the shortening and 1 cup sugar. Beat in the molasses and egg.
Whisk the flour, cinnamon, cloves, baking soda, ginger, and salt, then mix slowly into the wet ingredients.
Scoop with a medium ice cream scoop, roll in the 1/4 cup sugar, and flatten slightly.
Bake 12 at a time for 15 minutes.

notes: A copycat of the ginger molasses cookies sold at Silver Dollar City. Thick and delicious.

items: Preheat the oven to 375°F and spray a 9x9-inch baking dish.
Whisk the milk, applesauce, butter, and egg.
Stir in the oats, brown sugar, nuts, dried fruit, and baking powder.
Pour into the dish and bake 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Indian Butter Chicken

items: Pan-fry the chicken until cooked through, then cut into cubes.
In the same pan, sauté the onion and garlic in the butter until tender.
Put the onion mixture (with all the butter) into a blender with all the sauce ingredients except the cream. Blend until smooth.
Return the sauce to the pan, add the chicken, and simmer on low about 20 minutes.
Stir in the cream just before serving.
**Rice:** add the fennel when you start the rice. When it's done, fluff and stir in the carrots and peas.

tips: Round out the meal with Naan, Pakora, or Vegetable Korma.

items: 1 lb pork sausage, browned and drained
Boil the potatoes, celery, carrots, and onion 10–15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Drain.
In a large pot, melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook 1–2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the milk and cook, stirring, until thickened into a white sauce.
Stir in the cooked vegetables, corn, and sausage.
Season with salt and pepper, and thin with more milk if needed.

recipes.title: Hamburger Soup #2 (Big-Family Version)

items: 1 lb hamburger, browned, drained, and rinsed
Put everything except the tomato soup in a large pot.
Bring to a boil and cook 30 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the tomato soup and heat through. Remove the bay leaf.

notes: Mom stretched the original Hamburger Soup to feed the whole family when the kids were all at home.

recipes.title: Soft Gingerbread Cookies

items: 1 tsp flavoring extract, such as vanilla or orange
Royal icing or glaze, for decorating
Cream the shortening, butter, and sugar. Add the molasses, eggs, and extract and beat until light and fluffy.
Sift the flour, baking soda, salt, and spices into a separate bowl. Add to the wet mixture about 1 cup at a time.
Divide the dough into 3 pieces, wrap each in plastic, and chill 1–2 hours.
Roll the dough 1/4 inch thick on floured parchment and cut into shapes.
Freeze the cut cookies about 10 minutes before baking so they hold their shape.
Bake 6–8 minutes for small cookies, 8–10 for medium, or 10–15 for large.
Cool, then decorate with royal icing or glaze.

tips: Watch the first batch closely. Gingerbread doesn't visibly brown, and by the time it does, it's overbaked and hard.
notes: Mom was never a gingerbread fan until she tried these soft ones from Kindra.

recipes.title: Creamy Chicken Noodle Soup (Reames Classic)

items: 1 (24 oz) package Reames Homestyle Egg Noodles (frozen)
Bring the broth to a boil with the bay leaves.
Add the frozen noodles and cook 20 minutes, stirring often.
Add the parsley, thyme, pepper, onion, celery, and carrots. Simmer about 10 minutes, until tender.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a skillet, whisk in the flour, and cook 1–2 minutes.
Stir the cream into the soup and bring to a simmer. Whisk in the butter-flour mixture until thickened.
Remove the bay leaves, stir in the chicken, and heat through.

tips: Kindra swaps the celery and carrots for a bag of frozen green beans and a bag of frozen peas and carrots.
Serve with Sesame Chew Bread.
notes: Kindra made this for Mom and Dad, and they say it's amazing.

recipes.title: McKenzie's Perfect Caramels

items: In a heavy saucepan over medium heat, combine the butter, brown sugar, condensed milk, corn syrup, and salt. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
At 238°F, add the vanilla and turn off the burner. Keep stirring until it reaches 240°F, then remove from the heat.
Pour into the pan. Don't scrape the bottom of the saucepan unless you're sure it hasn't browned.
Cool completely. Turn out onto a cutting mat and cut into squares or strips with a sharp knife.
Wrap each piece in wax paper or 3x5 cellophane wrappers.

tips: **Chocolate-coated:** melt chocolate chips with a little canola oil, spread over the caramel, let dry, flip, and coat the other side before cutting.
**Tar Bar (licorice) option:** stir in 1 Tbsp anise oil and 1 tsp black paste food coloring instead of the vanilla.
notes: Dad got this recipe from McKenzie and has had great success with it.

recipes.title: Chocolate Orange Jelly Sticks

items: Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water to soften.
In a saucepan, stir the sugar into the hot water until dissolved. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Stir in the softened gelatin, turn to medium-low, and boil gently 20 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the orange juice concentrate, lemon juice, extracts, and food coloring.
Pour into the pan and let stand overnight.
Cut into narrow sticks. Melt the chocolate and dip the sticks, then let set.

notes: Part of the family's Christmas candy table, a tradition inspired by Elsie Jean "Gale" Thackeray. Orange sticks are hard to find in the Midwest, so Dad mastered making them.

recipes.title: Wassail (Hot Spiced Apple Cider)

items: Boil the sugar and water for 2 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Add the cloves, allspice, cinnamon, and ginger (tying them in a cheesecloth bag makes them easy to remove). Cover and let steep 1 hour.
Remove the spices. Add the orange juice, lemon juice, and cider, bring quickly to a boil, and serve hot.

notes: Sharon Lyons' recipe (Brittany's mother-in-law). Blake still remembers his first taste at her house as the best wassail ever.

recipes.title: Homemade Marshmallows

items: 1/4 cup powdered sugar mixed with 1/4 cup cornstarch
In the bowl of a stand mixer with the whisk attachment, sprinkle the gelatin over 1/2 cup cold water. Let it soften.
In a saucepan, stir the sugar, corn syrup, salt, and another 1/2 cup cold water just to combine. Cook over medium-high heat, swirling occasionally, to 240°F, about 10 minutes.
With the mixer on low, slowly pour the hot syrup into the gelatin. Mix until the gelatin dissolves, then add the vanilla.
Turn to high and whip about 10 minutes, until very thick, stiff, and white.
Spread in the pan. Let it set uncovered until firm, about 4 hours at room temperature or 2 hours in the fridge.
Sift a generous layer of the powdered sugar mixture onto the counter. Loosen the edges with a knife and pull the slab out onto the sugar (it's sticky but comes out in one piece).
Dust the top and cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes with a long, sharp knife, wiping it clean as needed.
Toss the cubes in more of the sugar mixture to coat all sides. Store airtight up to 4 days.

tips: **Peppermint:** add 1 tsp peppermint extract (skip the vanilla for pure mint) and fold in crushed peppermint.
**Chocolate-dipped:** dip in melted milk chocolate and let dry.
Drop one into hot chocolate or use them in s'mores.
notes: Dad has become a homemade marshmallow expert.

recipes.title: Homemade Clotted Cream

items: **Day 1:** preheat the oven to 170–180°F. Pour the cream into a wide, shallow baking dish so it's only 1–2 inches deep. Bake uncovered for 12 hours (overnight works well).
**Day 2:** a skin will have formed on top. Carefully take the dish out and let it cool to room temperature. Cover and refrigerate 8 hours or overnight.
**Day 3:** gently skim off the thick top layer, leaving the thin liquid behind. The skin is fine; it softens as you stir.
Stir the clotted cream gently until smooth. If it's too thick, stir in a little of the leftover liquid.
Store covered in the fridge up to 2 weeks, or freeze and thaw in the fridge.

tips: Serve on crumpets or English muffins with jam.
notes: Mom and Dad fell in love with crumpets, jam, and clotted cream on a trip to England.

recipes.title: Porcupine Meatballs

items: Mix the meatball ingredients (the rice goes in uncooked) and shape into balls. Arrange in a 9x13-inch pan.
Stir the sauce ingredients together and pour over the meatballs.
Cover and bake 1 hour, until the rice is tender.
Sprinkle with mozzarella if you like.

tips: **Stovetop:** brown the meatballs in a skillet, turning gently, then add the sauce and simmer about 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Southern Skillet Cornbread

items: Put the shortening in a black cast iron skillet and set it in the oven while it preheats to 350°F.
In a bowl, mix the cornmeal, eggs, and flour.
Pour some of the melted shortening from the skillet into the batter, then stir in buttermilk until it's like cake batter.
Pour into the hot skillet and bake 30 minutes.
Turn out onto a plate to cool.

tips: To make regular cornmeal self-rising, add 3 Tbsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt. White Lily is better, though.
This is a true Southern cornbread, not sweet.
notes: A family tradition. Mom crumbles it into a glass of milk and eats it with a spoon, just like her mother and grandfather did with buttermilk.

items: Rinse the okra, trim off the tips and stems, and slice into 1/4-inch rounds.
Beat the eggs with the salt, add the okra, and let soak 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a cast iron skillet to 375°F, hot enough that a drop of water pops.
Put the coating ingredients in a gallon zip-top bag.
Lift the okra out of the egg with a slotted spoon, shaking off the extra. Add to the bag and shake until well coated.
Fry in two batches until golden brown. Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with kosher salt.

recipes.title: Chicken-Fried Chicken

items: 4 chicken breasts, butterflied and pounded thin
Mix the coating ingredients in a gallon zip-top bag.
Shake the chicken in flour, dip it in the beaten egg, then shake in the coating bag until well covered.
Heat enough oil to cover the bottom of a nonstick skillet. Fry the chicken until golden on both sides.
Finish in the oven if needed, until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165–170°F.
Serve with mashed potatoes and white country gravy.

tips: **Oven option (untested):** bake the coated chicken in a 9x13 at 350°F for 45 minutes. Pour 1 stick melted butter over it and bake 5 minutes more.

recipes.title: Chicken Salad Wraps

items: Mix the chicken, fruit, pecans, apple, and celery.
Stir in just enough dressing to hold it together.
Spoon into warmed tortillas and roll up.

tips: Celery adds crunch if you don't have an apple.
Also good on any kind of bread or over lettuce.
Dad prefers a mayo-based dressing instead of ranch.

items: 8 oz pasta or ditalini, cooked and drained
3/4 cup finely diced green or red pepper

ingredients.heading: Dressing
items: 1 Tbsp red wine vinegar (or white or apple cider vinegar)
Rinse the cooked pasta under cold water and drain well.
Toss with the pepper, celery, onion, peas, cheese, and relish.
Whisk the dressing ingredients, pour over the salad, and stir to coat.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Pinwheel Candy

items: 4 Tbsp russet potato, peeled, cooked, and pushed through a fine strainer
Put the mashed potato in a bowl and start mixing in powdered sugar. At first it will turn almost liquid; keep adding sugar until it's firm enough to roll.
Roll it out on parchment into a rectangle.
Roll up like a cinnamon roll and slice thinly with a serrated knife.

notes: Mom searched more than 40 years for this treat. She ate one almost every day in the BYU–Hawaii cafeteria.

recipes.title: Dad's White Bread (plus Rolls and Silver Dollar City Cinnamon Bread)

steps.heading: Dough
items: In your mixer bowl, combine the warm water, sugar, oil, and yeast. Let stand 10–15 minutes, until frothy.
Add the salt and flour and mix.
Knead 5–6 minutes in a stand mixer (KitchenAid, Bosch, or similar). Don't cut the kneading short, and **don't add any extra flour**.
Drizzle a little oil around the dough and turn it with a rubber spatula to coat. Cover the bowl.
Warm the oven to 100–110°F (or use the proof setting), turn it off, and let the dough rise inside until doubled, about 1 hour.
Punch down with the spatula, let rise 30 minutes more, then punch down again.
Knead by hand 30–45 seconds to work out the air bubbles. Dad does this in the air, not on a floured counter.

steps.heading: Loaves
items: Divide into 2 equal pieces (about 710 g, or 25–26 oz, each).
Shape each into a tight loaf with your hands (no rolling pin), working out any bubbles and tucking the ends under.
Place in two well-greased **8x4-inch** loaf pans lined with sprayed parchment. This pan size gives tall loaves.
Let rise uncovered in the warm oven about 30 minutes, just until the dough reaches the top of the pans. Don't let it go higher.
Take the pans out and preheat the oven to 350°F. The loaves will rise about 1 inch above the pans while it heats.
Brush the tops with butter for a shine. Cool in the pans 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

steps.heading: Silver Dollar City cinnamon bread variation
items: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease three small (3x7-inch) foil loaf pans.
Divide the dough into 3 equal pieces (weigh for even loaves) and shape each into a loaf.
With kitchen scissors, snip deep cuts across each loaf without cutting all the way through.
Mix the brown sugar, white sugar, and cinnamon. Roll each loaf gently in the melted butter, then in the cinnamon sugar.
Arrange in the pans, sprinkle the remaining cinnamon sugar on top, and bake 30–35 minutes.
Stir the powdered sugar, vanilla, melted butter, and enough water to make a thin glaze, and drizzle over the warm loaves.

tips: Weigh the ingredients, especially the flour. Dad buys bread flour at Sam's Club.
A clear shower cap makes a handy, reusable bowl cover.
Dad uses this one dough for all his rolls, loaves, and cinnamon twist bread.

recipes.title: Easy Coconut Curry Chicken

items: 24 oz tomato sauce (or blended canned tomatoes)
Vegetables (optional): cubed unpeeled potato, chopped broccoli, sliced zucchini, sweet peas
Pan-fry the chicken breasts in a little oil until cooked, then cut into cubes.
Put the chicken in a large pot with all the other ingredients and any vegetables you like.
Simmer 30 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Serve over rice or cauliflower rice.

tips: Use whatever vegetables you have on hand.

recipes.title: Crunchy Granola

items: Preheat the oven to 275°F and line 2 baking sheets with parchment.
In a saucepan, stir the brown sugar and water over heat until the sugar dissolves. Stir in the vanilla and salt.
In a large bowl, combine the oats, pecans, almonds, and coconut. Pour the syrup over the top and mix thoroughly.
Spread on the baking sheets and bake 45 minutes to 1 hour, until golden.
Let cool completely, then stir in the raisins. Store airtight.

tips: Great as cereal or sprinkled over yogurt.

recipes.title: Thai Chicken Satay Noodle Salad with Coconut Peanut Dressing

ingredients.heading: Chicken
items: 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts or 6 thighs, cut into chunks

ingredients.heading: Noodle salad
items: 1/4 red cabbage, shredded (or a bag of coleslaw mix)
Whisk together the coconut milk, lime zest, peanut butter, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, oil, and sweet chili sauce.

Pour one-third of the sauce over the chicken and marinate 20–30 minutes. Stir the rice vinegar into the remaining two-thirds to thin it for the dressing. Keep the two separate; the marinade has touched raw chicken.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with foil, parchment, or a silicone mat.
Thread the chicken onto the soaked skewers and bake 20–25 minutes, until cooked through.
Cook the spaghetti according to the package, rinse with cold water, and drain.
Build each plate with pasta, chicken, and the cabbage, cucumber, bell pepper, carrots, and cilantro.
Drizzle with the dressing and top with chopped peanuts, plus red pepper flakes or hot sauce if you like.

notes: Whitney made this for Mom and Dad at her house in Denver in August 2020. They loved it.

items: 1 small onion, chopped (or 1/8 cup dried onion flakes)
Mix everything except the ketchup with your hands until combined. Press into a loaf pan.
Spread the ketchup over the top.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Toast the pecans on a baking sheet about 5 minutes, until crisp. Cool and chop.
Beat the butter and both sugars until light and fluffy. On low, add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Sift the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt and add slowly to the mixer.
Mix in the oats, raisins, and pecans.
Scoop with a 2-inch cookie scoop onto parchment-lined sheets and flatten slightly with a damp hand.
Bake 12–15 minutes, until lightly browned. Cool on a rack.

recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Butter Pecan Cookies

items: Melt the 2 Tbsp butter in a skillet and toast the pecans about 5 minutes. Set aside.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt.
In a mixer, beat the 2 sticks melted butter with both sugars. Beat in the egg, egg yolk, milk, and vanilla.
By hand, stir in the flour mixture just until combined, then the pecans and chocolate chips.
Cover and chill at least 1 hour; overnight is best.
Preheat the oven to 375°F and line baking sheets with parchment or silicone mats.
Scoop the dough and bake 9–11 minutes, until golden brown.
Cool on the sheet about 2 minutes, then move to a rack.

tips: **Freeze for later:** scoop the dough onto a sheet, freeze, then store in a zip-top bag. Thaw a bit and bake at 375°F until golden.

recipes.title: Camp Cedar Cereal Bars

items: 5 cups Fruity Pebbles or Rice Krispies
5 cups Cap'n Crunch with Crunch Berries
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Stir in the marshmallows with a wooden spoon until melted.
Stir in all the cereal until coated.
Press firmly into the dish, really packing it down.
Refrigerate until cold, then cut with a serrated knife.

notes: Rosemary Thackeray made these for the Thackeray family reunion at Camp Cedar, Utah. This version is close to hers. Great for Primary parties and ward or family barbecues.

recipes.title: Lyons Dinner Rolls

items: Stir the yeast and pinch of sugar into the warm water. Let stand 5–10 minutes, until foamy.
In a stand mixer, mix the eggs, 1/2 cup sugar, oil, and salt. Add the yeast mixture.
Mix in 3 cups of the flour, then add more 1/2 cup at a time until the dough starts to pull away from the sides of the bowl. Knead until smooth.
Place in a greased bowl, cover with a towel, and let rise until doubled, 1–1 1/2 hours.
Punch down. With floured hands, shape into balls a little bigger than a golf ball.
Arrange on a baking sheet about 1/2 inch apart so they rise into each other and stay soft on the sides. Cover and let rise until doubled, about 45 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Bake 25–30 minutes, until golden.
Brush the tops with melted butter and cool slightly before serving.

notes: Brittany shared this recipe, and it finally gave Mom dinner rolls she can count on. Dad still uses Grandma Elsie's recipe with great success.

recipes.title: Best Breakfast Cake Ever

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Generously grease a deep 9x13-inch pan.
Sift the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cream the butter and sugar. Add the flour mixture and the milk in alternating batches, mixing just until combined each time.
Gently fold in the beaten egg whites with a rubber spatula. Spread in the pan.
Cut the topping ingredients together with a pastry cutter or fork until clumpy and crumbly. Scatter over the batter.
Bake 40–45 minutes, until the center no longer jiggles. Serve warm.

notes: A Pioneer Woman recipe, shared by Brittany.

recipes.title: Glazed Cake Donuts ("Sprinkies")

ingredients.heading: Donuts
items: 1 large egg, room temperature, lightly beaten
4 cups vegetable oil (2–3 inches deep in your pan)

steps.heading: Dough
items: Sift the flour, sugar, baking powder, nutmeg, and salt into a large bowl.
Add the milk, egg, butter, and vanilla and stir until fully combined. The dough will be sticky.
On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough 3/4 to 1 inch thick. Cut with a donut cutter (or a 3 1/2-inch round cutter plus a 1-inch cutter for the holes). Set on a baking sheet.

steps.heading: Glaze
items: Whisk the confectioners' sugar, corn syrup, vanilla, and enough milk to make a thick, syrupy glaze.

steps.heading: Fry
items: Heat the oil to 350°F. Fry 1–2 donuts at a time, 45 seconds to 1 minute per side, until golden.
Drain on paper towels and let cool slightly.
Dip the tops in glaze and set on a rack over a baking sheet. Dip twice for a thicker coat.
**Chocolate glaze:** after glazing half the donuts, whisk the cocoa and milk into the remaining glaze and dip the rest.
Add sprinkles while the glaze is wet.

tips: No corn syrup? Mix 2 tsp sugar with 1 tsp hot water and use that instead.
notes: Candi made these for Slade, who calls cake donuts "sprinkies." The whole family gobbles them up, and the dough only needs an hour in the fridge.
Adapted from I Am Baker (iambaker.net/cake-donuts).

recipes.title: Brown Sugar Caramel Frosting

items: Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat.
Stir in the brown sugar and cook until it dissolves. Stir in the milk.
Remove from the heat and beat in the powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth.
If it's too thin, beat in more powdered sugar.

tips: Use it on Filled Cookies or banana cake.

recipes.title: Filled Cookies

steps.heading: Filling
items: Cook the raisins, sugar, flour, lemon juice, and water in a saucepan, stirring, until thick. Stir in the pecans and let cool.

steps.heading: Cookies
items: Sift the flour, baking powder, and salt. Cut in the butter until crumbly.
In another bowl, mix the sugar, eggs, baking soda, vanilla, and milk. Stir into the flour mixture.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Roll the dough 1/8 inch thick on a floured surface and cut into 2 1/2-inch circles.
Put 1 tsp filling on half the circles, top with the remaining circles, and pinch the edges to seal.
Bake 10–12 minutes, until light brown. Let cool.

steps.heading: Frosting
items: Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat. Stir in the brown sugar and cook until dissolved. Add the milk.
Remove from the heat and beat in the powdered sugar and vanilla. Add more powdered sugar if it's too thin.

notes: Dad's favorite cookie. His mother made them especially for him.

items: 1 lb chicken breast, cut into pieces
Mix the mustard, olive oil, lemon zest and juice, salt, pepper, garlic, and rosemary.
Add the chicken and toss. Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes or overnight.
Thread onto skewers and grill until cooked through.
1 1/2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese, divided
Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Mince the garlic and sauté with the onion in a little butter or olive oil until soft.
Let the hash browns thaw slightly. In a large bowl, mix them with the sour cream, soup, Parmesan, 1 cup of the cheddar, the onion mixture, and salt and pepper.
Spread in the pan and sprinkle with the remaining 1/2 cup cheddar.
Melt the butter, toss with the cornflakes, and scatter over the top.
Bake 50–60 minutes, until golden and bubbly.
Preheat the oven to 375°F. Spray a cooling rack and set it on a baking sheet.
Mix the Parmesan, thyme, oregano, basil, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt.
Arrange the zucchini on the rack, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with the Parmesan mixture.
Bake 15 minutes, then broil 2–3 minutes, until crisp and golden. Serve right away.

recipes.title: Greek Yogurt Bagels

items: 1 cup nonfat Greek yogurt (Fage is best)
Toppings: everything bagel seasoning, poppy seeds, or sesame seeds
Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line a baking sheet with greased parchment or a silicone mat.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, and yogurt into a dough.
Knead on a floured surface about 15 times.
Divide into 4 balls. Roll each into a 3/4-inch-thick rope and join the ends into a ring.
Brush with the beaten egg white and sprinkle both sides with your favorite topping.

tips: The same dough works for calzones, pizza crust, or breadsticks.
notes: From Whitney. High in protein, easy, and delicious.

items: Cream the shortening, sugars, peanut butter, eggs, and vanilla.
Mix in the flour, baking soda, and salt.
Roll into balls and flatten with a fork dipped in water or sugar.
Bake 11–13 minutes. Mom waits until the edges are light brown for crunchy edges.

recipes.title: Apple Crisp Topping

items: Mix everything together with a fork or your fingers until crumbly.
Sprinkle over the fruit filling in a baking dish.
Bake 40 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

tips: Mom often doubles or triples the topping because it's the best part.

items: Powdered sugar, cinnamon sugar, or pie filling, for topping
Heat a few inches of oil to 370°F.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, egg, milk, and salt into a smooth batter.
Hold your finger over the bottom of a funnel and fill it with batter.
Over the hot oil, release your finger and move the funnel in a spiral so the batter drizzles into a lacy circle.
Fry until golden, turning once with tongs. Drain on paper towels.
Dust with powdered sugar or cinnamon sugar, or top with pie filling and powdered sugar.

recipes.title: Coconut Chew Bars

items: Mix the crust ingredients and press into an ungreased 9x13-inch pan. Bake 12–15 minutes.
Mix the filling ingredients and pour over the baked crust. Bake 20 minutes more.
Beat the frosting ingredients until smooth, spread over the bars, and cut.

notes: One of Grandma Elsie's favorites at Thackeray picnics in Etna, California.

recipes.title: Snickerdoodles

items: Beat the shortening, sugar, eggs, vanilla, and almond extract.
Mix in the cream of tartar, baking soda, salt, and flour.
Roll into balls, roll in cinnamon sugar, and set on baking sheets.
Bake 9 minutes. They'll finish flattening as they cool.

notes: Recipe from Joe Rogers.

items: 1 yellow or pineapple cake mix (plus ingredients listed on the box)
1 (20 oz) can pineapple slices or crushed pineapple, drained
Melt the butter in the bottom of a 9x13-inch pan. Sprinkle the brown sugar evenly over it.
Arrange the pineapple over the brown sugar.
Mix the cake batter according to the box and pour it over the pineapple.
Bake 43–48 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes, then turn out onto a serving platter.

ingredients.heading: Potatoes and sauce
items: 20 small potatoes, or 5–7 potatoes peeled and cut in chunks
Mix all the meatball ingredients, roll into 1-inch balls, and set on a baking sheet. Bake 15 minutes.
Put the meatballs and potatoes in a 9x13-inch pan.
Mix the soups, sour cream, and seasoned salt and spread over the top.
Cover and bake 1–1 1/2 hours, until the potatoes are tender.
Sugar, cinnamon sugar, powdered sugar, or glaze, for coating
Combine the flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, nutmeg, and baking soda.
Add the 1/4 cup oil, buttermilk, and egg and beat with a fork until smooth.
Drop the batter by tablespoons into the hot oil and fry about 3 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Drain briefly, then roll in sugar, cinnamon sugar, or powdered sugar, or dip in glaze.
Preheat the oven to 375°F and grease a muffin tin.
Melt the butter. Combine the flour, sugar, lemon peel, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Whisk the yogurt, butter, egg, and lemon juice, then stir into the dry ingredients until barely combined.
Fill the muffin cups and bake about 20 minutes.
**Glaze:** stir the rest of the lemon juice and a little grated peel with enough powdered sugar to make a pourable glaze.
Poke the warm muffins with a fork and pour the glaze over them.

recipes.title: Kim's Sauce

items: 1/4 cup liquid egg substitute (not raw egg)
Refrigerate everything except the sugar for about 1 hour so it's well chilled.
Put the oil, vinegar, ketchup, dry mustard, salt, and egg substitute in a blender and blend well.
With the blender running, gradually add the sugar and blend until the sauce is thick and emulsified.

tips: Use it on everything: egg rolls, salads, Sticky Rice, any Chinese food, or teriyaki chicken.
notes: A copycat of the famous dipping sauce from Kim's, a Chinese restaurant in Medford, Oregon, that has since closed. The family first had it with egg rolls. Grandma Elsie and Dad spent hours recreating it. Submitted by Mom.

recipes.title: Sticky Rice

items: **Rice cooker:** cook on the regular rice setting.
**Stovetop:** bring the water to a boil, add the rice and salt, then cover, reduce the heat, and simmer 20 minutes.
Serve with Kim's Sauce, a fish sauce dip, or your favorite sauce.

tips: Sweet rice is also called sticky rice, glutinous rice, or malagkit. Despite the name, it has no gluten. Look for it in grocery stores or Asian markets.
notes: A staple of Northern Thai and Lao cooking. One of Dad's favorites.

recipes.title: Lyons Monkey Bread

items: 1 package cook-and-serve butterscotch pudding (not instant), dry
Grease a Bundt pan and arrange the frozen rolls in it.
Melt the butter and stir in the brown sugar and dry pudding mix. Pour over the rolls.
In the morning, bake at 325°F for 1 hour.
While warm, turn out onto a serving plate.

notes: A Lyons family Christmas morning tradition.

recipes.title: Caramel Topping for Pecan Cinnamon Rolls

items: Heat everything in a saucepan about 2 minutes, until the sugar dissolves.
Pour into the bottom of the baking dish.
Set unbaked cinnamon rolls on top and let them rise.
Bake as directed for the cinnamon rolls.
Turn the pan upside down onto a platter as soon as it comes out of the oven.

tips: Pairs with Mom and Dad's Cinnamon Rolls.

recipes.title: Elsie's Whole Wheat Muffins

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a muffin tin.
Whisk the milk, eggs, and oil.
Stir in the flour, brown sugar, baking powder, salt, and raisins just until combined.
Fill the muffin cups and bake about 15 minutes.
While warm, dip the tops in melted butter, then in cinnamon sugar.

notes: Grandma Elsie's recipe.

items: Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the zucchini until lightly browned.
Push the zucchini to the side and sauté the onion and garlic until golden.
Sprinkle with the basil and sugar and stir-fry until the zucchini is crisp-tender.
Stir in the tomatoes just to heat through. Season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with Parmesan if you like.
Chill at least 1 hour before serving.
Mix the green beans, water chestnuts, soup, milk, salt, pepper, and half the fried onions in a baking dish.
Bake 30 minutes, topping with the remaining onions for the last 5 minutes.
1 cup semisweet or milk chocolate chips
Preheat the oven to 375°F and grease a cookie sheet.
Mix the flour, sugar, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Beat in the softened butter until crumbly.
Add the banana, egg, and oats and mix well. Stir in the chocolate chips and nuts.
Drop by spoonfuls onto the sheet.
Bake 13–15 minutes, then cool on a rack.

recipes.title: Warm Spiced Coconut Milk

items: Heat over medium, stirring, until warm. Don't let it boil.

notes: An Indian-style warm milk. The kids who love Indian food ask Dad to make it in the evenings.

recipes.title: Pakora (Indian Fried Vegetables)

items: Dice all the vegetables to about the size of a pea.
Whisk the batter ingredients until it's about as thick as pancake batter. For thicker batter, add flour 1 Tbsp at a time.
Stir in 4 cups of the diced vegetables.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Drop the batter in by spoonfuls and fry until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and salt to taste.

tips: Any mix of vegetables works.

recipes.title: Beef Carrot Casserole

items: 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese (for the top)
Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Brown the beef. Add the onion and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomato sauce, salt, and pepper. Simmer uncovered 5 minutes.
In a bowl, combine the sour cream, cottage cheese, parsley, carrots, and noodles.
Layer in the pan, starting and ending with the noodle mixture: noodles, meat, noodles.
Bake 30 minutes, adding the cheddar for the last 5 minutes.

tips: Freezes well. Bake from frozen at 400°F for 1 hour.
notes: One of Dad's favorites, maybe because it's a bit like lasagna.

items: 1 German chocolate cake mix (plus ingredients listed on the box)
Bake the cake in a 9x13-inch pan according to the box.
While it's warm, poke holes all over it with the handle of a wooden spoon.
Pour the sweetened condensed milk over the cake, then the butterscotch and caramel toppings. Sprinkle with toffee bits.
Frost with Cool Whip, sprinkle with coconut, drizzle with chocolate syrup, and finish with more toffee bits. Refrigerate.

recipes.title: Oreo Dessert

items: Set aside 12 cookies for the topping. Crush the rest.
Melt the butter, mix with the crushed cookies, and press into a 9x13-inch pan.
Beat the cream cheese, pudding mix, and milk until fluffy. Spread over the crust.
Spread the Cool Whip on top and refrigerate 6 hours.
Crush the reserved 12 cookies and sprinkle over the top before serving.

notes: Slade William's birthday cake request every year.

items: Mix the crust ingredients and press into a 9x13-inch glass dish. Bake 15 minutes.
Beat the eggs, lemon juice, flour, and sugar on high for 2 minutes. Pour over the hot crust.
Sift powdered sugar over the top. Let cool completely before cutting.

recipes.title: Pasta e Fagioli (Olive Garden Style)

items: 1 cup ditalini pasta or mini shells
1 (15 oz) can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15 oz) can Great Northern beans, drained and rinsed
Cook the pasta, drain, and set aside.
In a large pot, brown the hamburger in the olive oil.
Mince the garlic. Add it to the pot with the onion, carrots, and celery and cook 3–5 minutes.
Stir in the broth, tomato sauce, diced tomatoes, basil, oregano, thyme, and 1 cup water. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the pasta and beans and heat through. Serve right away.

notes: McKenzie started making this for the family in high school. The family loves Olive Garden's soups.

recipes.title: Poppy Seed Bread with Orange Glaze

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease the loaf pans very well.
Beat all the bread ingredients together for 2 minutes.
Fill the pans about half full and bake about 45 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
While the bread bakes, heat the glaze ingredients in a saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the glaze over the hot loaves and let them cool in the pans.

tips: Small disposable foil loaf pans make these easy to give as gifts.
notes: One of Mom's favorite Christmas gifts to give.

recipes.title: Cheese Tortellini Soup

items: 1/2 bag chopped spinach or 1/2 bag frozen peas
In a large pot, sauté the onion and garlic in the butter until soft.
Add the bouillon, basil, parsley, salt, and water and bring to a boil.
Add the tortellini and cook 10–12 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and the spinach or peas and heat through.

tips: Serve with garlic French bread toast.
notes: Mom and Dad had this soup at a little restaurant in Yreka, and Dad recreated it at home. A family favorite.

recipes.title: Elsie's Chocolate Éclairs

ingredients.heading: Filling
items: Cook-and-serve vanilla pudding, prepared and chilled
Bring the water to a boil and add the butter, stirring until melted.
Add the flour and salt all at once. Stir constantly over the heat until the dough pulls into a ball around the spoon.
Remove from the heat and cool 2–3 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then keep beating until the dough is smooth and shiny.
Pipe or spoon into éclair shapes on a baking sheet.
Bake 10 minutes, then lower the oven to 325°F and bake 10 minutes more. Cool.
Split each éclair and fill with vanilla pudding.
Beat cocoa, powdered sugar, and butter with enough milk to make a smooth frosting, and spread over the tops.

notes: Slade and Dad have gotten really good at these. When Dad makes a big batch of pudding, he calls Slade as a hint to come make the éclairs.

recipes.title: Chevy's Red Rice

items: 1/2 tsp chipotle purée (up to 2 tsp for more heat)
1 Tbsp chopped cilantro or 1 tsp dried
Blend the tomatoes with the chipotle purée, then stir in the cilantro.
In a large bowl, combine the tomato mixture with the water, garlic, and salt.
Heat the oil in a large pot over high heat until it's almost smoking.
Add the rice and onion and sauté 7–10 minutes, until most of the grains turn bright white or light golden. Don't drain the oil.
Pour in the tomato mixture and simmer about 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from the heat, cover, and let stand 20–30 minutes, stirring and tasting every 10 minutes, until tender.
Fluff with a fork and keep warm until serving.

tips: **Don't skip the chipotle.** It's where the smoky flavor comes from. Make it by blending a can of chipotles in adobo until smooth; extra keeps in the freezer up to a year.
The original recipe uses 2 tsp chipotle purée. Julie uses 1/2 tsp for flavor without much heat.
Julie usually doubles it. It keeps well and makes great leftovers.
notes: A must for any Mexican feast.

recipes.title: Julie's Guacamole

items: 2 cloves garlic or 1 tsp garlic powder
Halve and pit the avocados and scoop into a bowl.
Add everything else and mash together, leaving it chunky.
Taste with a chip and adjust salt, pepper, and lime.

tips: This is a starting point. Use up to 1/2 onion or more garlic if you like.

recipes.title: Easy Cream Cheese Pesto Dip

items: Set the block of cream cheese in the center of a piece of foil and pour the pesto over the top.
Wrap the foil loosely around it, set it on an oven-safe dish, and bake 15–20 minutes, until soft all the way through.
Open the foil, sprinkle with tomato and mozzarella, and broil until the cheese is browned. Watch closely.
Serve with pretzel thins (the best), pita chips, or veggies.

notes: A guaranteed hit at get-togethers. One of Julie's friends literally licks the foil clean every time.

recipes.title: Potato Soup with Homemade Noodles

items: 5 large potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Boil the potatoes in salted water.
Meanwhile, mix the flour, egg, salt, and pepper into a stiff noodle dough.
Before the potatoes are fully done, drop the dough into the boiling pot in small spoonfuls.
When the potatoes are tender, pour off some of the water if it seems like too much.
Stir in the butter and milk.
Mix the cornstarch with the warm water and stir it in to thicken.

tips: Love the noodles? Double the noodle dough.
notes: A cozy, budget-friendly soup.

items: 1 box Jiffy cornbread mix (plus 1 egg and 1/3 cup milk)
In an oven-safe skillet or pan, brown the beef with the green pepper and onion. Drain, then stir in the taco seasoning.
Stir in the beans and corn and spread in a baking dish (or leave in the oven-safe skillet).
Mix the cornbread mix with the egg and milk and spread over the top.
Bake 20 minutes, sprinkling with cheddar for the last 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Layered Green Salad

items: In a clear glass bowl if you have one, layer the drained water chestnuts, then the celery.
Break apart the frozen peas (don't cook them) and spread them over the celery.
Toss the lettuce and green onions together and layer over the peas.
Spread mayonnaise over the top like frosting a cake, sealing it all the way to the edges.
Sprinkle with the sugar and Parmesan.
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight.

notes: A traditional Christmas salad Julie still makes every year.
Recipe by Jane Friden.

recipes.title: Tar Bars (Licorice Caramels)

items: 1 tsp anise oil (not extract), or 5 tsp anise extract
1 tsp black paste food coloring (not liquid)
In a heavy saucepan, combine the condensed milk, sugar, butter, salt, and corn syrup. Cook, stirring constantly, to 234°F.
Remove from the heat and stir in the anise oil and black food coloring.
Pour into the dish and let cool completely.
To release it, dip the bottom of the dish in hot water for a few seconds. Turn the candy out onto a buttered counter.
With a buttered sharp knife, cut into strips, then into pieces. Wrap each in wax paper or plastic wrap.

tips: The right temperature depends on elevation. This recipe was developed in Etna in Northern California, and some cooks go to 240°F.
notes: A famous Thackeray treat, like a caramel but licorice. The family used to buy "Tar Bars" at The Nut Tree in Vacaville, California, a regular stop on the way to the Oakland Temple.
Mom believes the recipe came from Uncle Ralph Thackeray.

recipes.title: Kerry's Lasagna

ingredients.heading: Meat sauce
items: 1/4 cup + 2 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley, divided

steps.heading: Sauce
items: In a large pot over medium heat, cook the sausage and beef, breaking them into small crumbles.
Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring often, until the meat is well browned.
Stir in the sugar, basil, fennel, oregano, 1/2 tsp salt, pepper, and 1/4 cup of the parsley.
Add the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, tomato sauce, and broth. Bring to a simmer, then turn to low and simmer 1–4 hours, stirring now and then. The longer, the better.

steps.heading: Noodles and filling
items: About 30 minutes before assembling, lay the uncooked noodles in a pan and cover them completely with very hot tap water. Soak 30 minutes, then drain.
Mix the cottage cheese, egg, the remaining 2 Tbsp parsley, 1/2 tsp salt, and nutmeg. Refrigerate until needed.

steps.heading: Assemble and bake
items: Preheat the oven to 375°F and lightly grease a deep 9x13-inch pan.
Spread about 1 cup meat sauce in the pan. Add 4 noodles, one-third of the cheese filling, one-quarter of the mozzarella, about 1 1/2 cups sauce, and 1/4 cup Parmesan.
Repeat to make three full layers.
Finish with a layer of noodles, 1 cup sauce, and the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan.
Tent loosely with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 25 minutes more, until the cheese is browned. Serve hot.

tips: Dad makes homemade noodles, which makes it even better, but store-bought noodles work fine.
Julie considers the fennel a must, but skip it if you don't like the flavor.
Serve with Aunt NaTel's French Bread.
notes: An A+ lasagna. It's Garrison's most-requested meal, and even Chase, who doesn't like lasagna, loves this one.

recipes.title: Grandma Elsie's Honey Butter

items: Refrigerate the honey, butter, mixing bowl, and beaters for at least 1 hour.
Beat the honey and butter together until smooth.

notes: Elsie Thackeray's recipe. A must with rolls at Thanksgiving.

recipes.title: Jarvis Chocolate Bundt Cake

items: 1 Betty Crocker Hershey's milk chocolate cake mix
Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a Bundt pan.
Mix the cake mix, pudding mix, water, oil, sour cream, and eggs until smooth. Stir in the chocolate chips.
Pour into the pan and bake 53 minutes to 1 hour.
**The secret:** turn the hot cake out and put it straight into a tightly covered cake keeper (like Tupperware). Let it "sweat" for 2 hours. This makes it incredibly moist.

notes: A woman in Mom's Lincolnton ward was famous for this cake.

recipes.title: Pistachio (Watergate) Salad

items: Gently fold everything together in a large bowl.

notes: Doug's Thanksgiving favorite. Mom grew up calling it Watergate salad. It's on the sweet side.

recipes.title: North Carolina Baked Ziti

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Brown the hamburger with the onion, drain, and stir in the spaghetti sauce.
Boil the ziti until tender and drain.
Layer in the pan: half the ziti, the provolone slices, the sour cream, and half the meat sauce.
Add the rest of the ziti, the shredded mozzarella, and the remaining sauce. Top with Parmesan.

notes: When Mom lived in Lincolnton, North Carolina, this was the favorite casserole to take to families in need.

items: Brown the hamburger with the onion and garlic salt. Drain.
Drain the green beans, stir them into the meat, and spread in a 9x13-inch pan.
Peel and thinly slice the potatoes and layer them over the meat.
Mix the soup and milk and spread over the potatoes. Sprinkle with cheddar.
Cover and bake 45 minutes to 1 hour, until the potatoes are fork-tender.

recipes.title: Dad's Chicken Tikka Masala

ingredients.heading: Sauce
items: 1/2 inch fresh ginger, grated (or 1 tsp ground ginger)
1 Tbsp fresh lime or lemon juice
1/4–1/2 cup chopped cilantro, or to taste
1 small can mild diced tomatoes with chiles
Salt, pepper, and sugar, to taste
Basmati rice and fresh cilantro, for serving
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and sauté until cooked through.
In another pan, sauté the garlic, ginger, and onion in the butter until tender.
Put the sautéed onion mixture in a blender with the lime juice, cilantro, turmeric, cumin, brown sugar, garam masala, tomato paste, and tomatoes. Blend until smooth.
Pour into a pan and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the cream and chicken and simmer 15–20 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper, and sugar, and thicken if needed. Add the red pepper if you like it hotter.
Serve over basmati rice, sprinkled with fresh cilantro.

tips: **Butter chicken:** stir in 1/4 cup butter.
Fennel, peas, and shaved carrots are nice cooked into the rice.
notes: Dad's recipe.

recipes.title: Almond Roca (Knapp Style)

items: Spread the 2 cups slightly chopped almonds over a jelly roll pan.
Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan. Add the sugar and stir constantly over medium-high heat until it reaches a full boil.
Keep cooking and stirring about 12 minutes, until it reaches 300°F (hard crack) on a candy thermometer and is golden brown, about the color of peanut butter.
Immediately pour over the almonds and spread evenly.
While the toffee is hot, scatter the chocolate chips over the top. Let them melt, then spread smooth with a frosting spatula.
Sprinkle with the 3/4 cup finely chopped almonds.
Let cool for several hours, then break into pieces.

notes: Whitney got this from her mother-in-law and made it for the family one Christmas. Mom calls it the best toffee she's ever had.

recipes.title: Best Ever Chunky Beef Stew

items: Cut the beef into bite-size chunks and toss with the flour to coat.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium. Brown the beef in two batches, leaving it alone so it gets a good crust. It doesn't need to cook through. Set it aside.
Cut the onion into wedges and mince the garlic. Sauté in the same pot 2–3 minutes. Move on quickly if the bottom starts to get too dark.
Stir in the tomato paste and broth, scraping up all the browned bits. Return the beef with the bay leaf, thyme, rosemary, and plenty of pepper.
Cover and bring to a simmer, then turn to low and simmer 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and slice the carrots and cut the potatoes into 3/4-inch cubes.
Add the carrots, potatoes, and peas. Cover and simmer 15–20 minutes more, until tender.
Stir in the Worcestershire, then season with salt and pepper. Remove the bay leaf, sprinkle with chopped parsley, and serve hot.

tips: Beef bouillon concentrate plus water is a cheaper alternative to canned broth.
notes: From Budget Bytes.

recipes.title: Kindra's Perfect "Shape-Holding" Sugar Cookies

ingredients.heading: Royal icing (makes 5 cups)
items: 2–3 tsp oil-free vanilla extract or emulsion

steps.heading: Cookies
items: Whisk the flour and salt together.
In another bowl, beat the butter and sugar until smooth and creamy. Beat in the egg and vanilla, then mix in the flour.
Wrap the dough in plastic and refrigerate.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Roll the dough 1/4 inch thick and cut into shapes.

steps.heading: Royal icing
items: Stir the vanilla into about half the water.
With the paddle attachment, briefly mix the confectioners' sugar and meringue powder.
On the lowest speed, slowly pour in the vanilla water, then keep adding water a little at a time until the icing looks like thick honey. You may not need all of it.
Turn to medium and whip 2–4 minutes, just until thick, fluffy, and holding a soft peak. Watch closely; timing varies.

tips: These cookies keep their shape, so they're perfect for decorating.
For a softer icing that won't crack, cut the meringue powder in half. It takes about a day to dry.
A fan helps the icing dry smooth and shiny. You can also experiment with a little corn syrup, glycerin, or cream of tartar.

recipes.title: Grandma Elsie's Spiral Pasta Salad

ingredients.heading: Dressing
items: 2/3 cup red wine vinegar (other vinegars are fine)
Cook the noodles, drain, and rinse under cold water.
Toss with the celery, tomatoes, and olives.
Whisk the dressing ingredients until the sugar dissolves. Pour over the salad and toss.

notes: Grandma Elsie Thackeray's recipe.

recipes.title: Dad's Oven "Dutch Oven" Chicken

items: 1 Tbsp Season-All (or 1/2 Tbsp salt and 1/2 Tbsp pepper)
4 carrots, cut in 3-inch lengths and halved
1 can cream of chicken soup mixed with 1/2 cup milk
Preheat the oven to 300°F (or 350°F if you're short on time).
Put the flour and Season-All in a gallon zip-top bag.
Cut each breast in half or thirds and shake in the flour until well coated. Save the leftover flour.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken well on both sides. It doesn't need to cook through.
In a 9x13-inch pan, layer half the onions, potatoes, and carrots. Lay the chicken on top, then add the rest of the vegetables.
Sprinkle the leftover flour over everything. It makes a nice thick gravy.
Pour the soup and milk mixture over the top.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 3 hours at 300°F or 2 hours at 350°F.

tips: Dad often uses two cans of soup for extra gravy.
notes: Dad's Dutch oven chicken adapted for a regular oven. It turned out perfect.

recipes.title: Perfect Chocolate Brownies

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Spray a 9x13-inch pan, line it with parchment if you like, and spray again.
Melt the chocolate, sugar, and butter together (the microwave works). Let cool.
Whisk the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt.
Beat the eggs and vanilla until foamy (room-temperature eggs foam best).
Mix the cooled chocolate into the eggs until well combined.
Fold in the flour mixture in two additions.
Spread in the pan and bake 22–25 minutes, until a toothpick comes out barely moist. Don't overbake.

tips: Half milk and half dark chocolate works if you're out of semisweet.
Brittany's favorite version adds a layer of York Peppermint Patties and homemade chocolate frosting.
notes: After years of searching, Brittany found a scratch brownie that beats her favorite boxed mix: dense, moist, crackly on top, and good right to the edges.
From the *Cuisine at Home* annual cookbooks.

recipes.title: Vegetable Korma

items: 1 (4 oz) can tomato sauce (or sauce from Chicken Tikka Masala)
2–3 cups frozen or fresh vegetables you enjoy
Heat the oil in a large skillet. Sauté the onion and potato until the potato is tender.
Add the ginger and garlic and sauté 1 minute.
Stir in the cream, tomato sauce, salt, sugar, and curry powder.
Add the vegetables. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer 10 minutes.

tips: Dad likes peas, cauliflower, carrots, sugar snap peas, and broccoli.

recipes.title: Wienies and Rice

items: Cook rice to serve with it.
In a skillet, stir together the flour, ketchup, vinegar, sugar, and mustard.
Stir in the water 1/4 cup at a time until smooth.
Add the hot dogs and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Simmer 5–10 minutes.

tips: The original recipe uses 1 Tbsp vinegar.
Brittany triples it for herself and four kids, and there are rarely leftovers.
notes: You'll either love it or hate it. Brittany's kids love it; her husband isn't convinced.

recipes.title: Kerry's Jerky

items: Put everything in a stand mixer with the paddle attachment and mix well.
Roll the meat out into a thin, even sheet and cut into strips.
Dry in a dehydrator (or smoker) until firm and leathery.

tips: Use 1 Tbsp liquid smoke for mild flavor or 2 Tbsp for more. Leave it out entirely if you're using a smoker.
Add more pepper for more bite, or ghost pepper, cayenne, or habanero for real heat.
Try other flavors like teriyaki.
notes: Dad's recipe.

recipes.title: Neesha's Best-Ever Caramel Popcorn

items: 25–30 cups popped popcorn (1–1 1/4 cups kernels, or 4–6 bags)
Put the popped popcorn in a very large bowl (or two).
In a heavy saucepan, bring the corn syrup, brown sugar, and salt to a boil.
Stir in the butter and sweetened condensed milk and cook to 228°F.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Pour over the popcorn and stir with a spatula until well coated. **The caramel is extremely hot**, so don't use your hands yet.
To make popcorn balls, let it cool slightly, spray your hands with cooking spray, and shape into balls.

notes: In the Russell family these are known as Neesha's Best-Ever Caramel Popcorn Balls.

recipes.title: Orange Chicken

steps.heading: Chicken
items: Set up three bowls: cornstarch mixed with the salt and pepper; the beaten eggs; and the bread crumbs.
Dip each piece of chicken in egg, then cornstarch, then egg again, then bread crumbs.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 360°F over medium heat. Fry the chicken in batches 2–3 minutes, until cooked through. Drain on paper towels.

steps.heading: Sauce
items: In a large saucepan over medium heat, stir together the 3 cups water, orange juice, rice vinegar, and soy sauce.
Stir in the brown sugar, orange zest, ginger, garlic, and red pepper flakes and bring to a boil.
Mix the cornstarch with the 4 Tbsp water until smooth. Slowly stir it into the boiling sauce until thickened.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and garnish with green onions.

tips: **Lighter version:** skip the breading. Season bite-size chicken with salt and pepper and cook it in a skillet with 2 Tbsp oil, then add the sauce. You may not need all of it.

recipes.title: Brittany's Berry Ice Cream Dessert

items: 1 box Danish Dessert (near the puddings), or premade fruit glaze from the produce section
1 lb strawberries (or blackberries, raspberries, or blueberries)
Melt the butter and stir in the Rice Krispies, brown sugar, coconut, and nuts.
Press half the crunchy mixture into a 9x13-inch pan.
Cut the ice cream into 1-inch slices and lay them over the crust.
Sprinkle the rest of the crunchy mixture on top. Freeze 1–2 hours.
Prepare the Danish Dessert according to the package and stir in the sliced berries.
Spoon the berry mixture over the top before serving.

tips: Double the crunchy mixture for extra crunch.
A drizzle of caramel on top is a nice addition.

recipes.title: Alana's Sugar Cookies (Lofthouse Copycat)

items: Cream the shortening and sugar. Beat in the milk, vanilla, and eggs.
Sift together the flour, salt, and baking powder. Add to the wet ingredients a little at a time, mixing until all the flour is in.
Roll out on a floured surface 1/4 to 1/2 inch thick and cut into shapes.
Bake about 15 minutes. Cool, then frost with buttercream.

tips: Kindra's Buttercream Icing works well here.
notes: Mom's favorite sugar cookie for 30 years, and better than the grocery-store version.

recipes.title: Best Lemon Water Ever

items: In a large drink dispenser or cooler, stir the sugar, lemon extract, and citric acid into the water until dissolved.
Add the ice and serve cold.

tips: Dad sometimes uses Splenda instead of sugar.
notes: Great for parties and Sunday dinners.

items: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the 1/2 cup warm water and let it sit while you continue.
In a large bowl, beat the hot water, salt, oil, and 3 cups of the flour well with a spoon.
Add the remaining 3 cups flour and the yeast mixture and beat well.
Let the dough rest 10 minutes, then stir it down. Repeat this rest-and-stir 5 times.
Divide in half. On a floured surface, roll each half into a 12x14-inch rectangle, then roll up into a loaf. Place on an oiled baking sheet.
Brush with beaten egg white and cut diagonal slashes 2–3 inches apart with a serrated knife.
Let rise 30 minutes. Bake at 375°F for 30 minutes, until golden.

recipes.title: Broiled Tilapia Parmesan

items: 2 Tbsp olive oil or softened butter
Preheat the broiler. Line a broiler pan or rimmed baking sheet with foil and spray with cooking spray.
Mix the Parmesan, oil, mayonnaise, lemon juice, basil, pepper, onion powder, and celery salt. If it's too thick to spread, add a little more oil or lemon juice.
Lay the fish on the pan in a single layer. Broil a few inches from the heat 4–5 minutes. Flip and broil 4–5 minutes more.
Spread about 1 Tbsp topping on each fillet and broil about 2 minutes, until browned and the fish flakes easily.

tips: With freshly grated Parmesan, use only 1/3 cup, and microwave the topping 15–30 seconds to smooth it.
The topping keeps in the fridge. Warm it 30 seconds in the microwave before using. It may freeze well too.
notes: From Julie's friend Nicole Moore, whose three young girls all love it. It won over most of Julie's family too, which is rare for fish. Try it if your kids resist fish.
Nicole serves it with quinoa.

recipes.title: Honey Lime Chicken Enchiladas

items: 2 cups Colby or Monterey Jack cheese, shredded
In a zip-top bag, mix the honey, lime juice, chili powder, and garlic powder. Add the chicken, toss, and marinate at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Spray a 9x13-inch pan (or two 8x8 pans).
Pour a thin layer of enchilada sauce over the bottom: about 1/2 can for a 9x13, or 1/3 can per 8x8.
Fill each tortilla with chicken and cheese, roll up, and place seam-side down in the pan.
Pour the remaining sauce over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake 30 minutes. Finish under the broiler for a few minutes until the cheese is golden and crisp.

tips: **Freezer meal:** assemble in two 8x8 pans and freeze one before baking. Bake from frozen, covered, at 350°F for 1 hour, then uncovered 30 minutes more. Or thaw overnight in the fridge and bake as usual.
notes: Easy enough for a weeknight, special enough for company.
Recipe from Mel's Kitchen Cafe.

recipes.title: Homemade Samoa Cookies

ingredients.heading: Coconut caramel topping
items: 8 oz dark, semisweet, or milk chocolate (chips are fine)

steps.heading: Cookies
items: Preheat the oven to 350°F and line baking sheets with parchment or silicone mats.
Cream the butter and sugar. On low speed, mix in the flour, baking powder, and salt, then the vanilla.
Add milk only if needed to form a soft, pliable dough that isn't sticky. Add a little flour if it's sticky.
Working in 2–3 batches, roll the dough between sheets of wax or parchment paper to about 1/4 inch thick.
Cut 1 1/2-inch rounds and place on the sheets. Cut a small hole in each center with a piping tip, a knife, or a wide straw. Re-roll scraps; this dough is forgiving.
Bake 10–12 minutes, until the bottoms are barely golden at the edges. Cool a few minutes on the pan, then on a rack.

steps.heading: Topping
items: Lower the oven to 300°F. Spread the coconut on a rimmed baking sheet and toast about 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until golden. It browns fast at the end, so watch closely. Let cool.
Microwave the caramels, milk, and salt on high 3–4 minutes, stirring a few times, until smooth. Fold in the coconut.
Spread 2–3 tsp topping on each cookie. Rewarm the caramel for a few seconds if it stiffens.

steps.heading: Chocolate
items: Melt the chocolate in 45-second bursts, stirring well each time (or use a double boiler).
Dip the bottom of each cookie in chocolate and set it on parchment.
Put the leftover chocolate in a zip-top bag, snip the corner, and drizzle stripes over the tops.
Let the chocolate set completely before storing airtight.

notes: A bit of work, but better than the boxed Girl Scout version, which keeps getting smaller.
Recipe from Once Upon a Plate.

recipes.title: Monster Cookies

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line baking sheets with parchment or silicone mats.
In a large bowl, mix the eggs and both sugars well.
Beat in the salt, vanilla, peanut butter, and butter.
Mix in the baking soda and oats.
Stir in the M&M's, chocolate chips, and raisins.
Let stand on the sheet about 3 minutes, then move to racks. Store airtight once cool.

notes: Peanut butter, chocolate, and oats in one chewy cookie.
Recipe by Paula Deen.

recipes.title: Samoa Brownies

items: 1 batch brownies (9x13) or a brownie mix
Bake the brownies in a 9x13-inch pan and let them cool completely.
**Toast the coconut:** spread it on a baking pan and bake at 400°F for 2–3 minutes. Stir, then bake 2–3 minutes more until golden. Watch closely so it doesn't burn.
In a large microwave-safe bowl, microwave the caramels, salt, and milk on high 3–5 minutes, stirring every 45–60 seconds, until smooth.
Stir in the toasted coconut and spread over the brownies.
Take out of the fridge at least 1 hour before cutting. Cut into bars.
Melt the chocolate chips and drizzle over the bars. Let set.

tips: Plan ahead: these need several hours to chill.
Store in the fridge, but let them sit out 20–30 minutes before serving so the caramel isn't too hard.
notes: Made for Girl Scout cookie season. Rich, and enough for a big group.
Recipe from Six Sisters' Stuff.

recipes.title: Saltine Toffee Squares

items: 12 oz milk chocolate chips, room temperature
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil and butter it (or spray with cooking spray).
Lay the saltines in a single layer to fill the pan.
Melt the butter and brown sugar in a saucepan and bring to a gentle boil. Turn to medium and boil 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour evenly over the crackers and bake 5 minutes.
Right away, sprinkle the chocolate chips over the top. Leave the pan in the oven, door propped, about 1 minute until the chips soften.
Spread the melted chocolate evenly. Sprinkle with nuts if you like (pecans are great).
Cut into squares while warm. Refrigerate about 30 minutes to set the chocolate, then store airtight.

notes: A Thackeray family classic that had somehow never made it onto the blog.
Recipe from Rose Hicks.

recipes.title: Panda Express Fried Rice

items: 1 cup long-grain rice, uncooked (or 2 cups freshly cooked)
1 cup frozen peas and carrots, thawed
1/8 tsp ground white pepper, or to taste
1 green onion, finely diced (including green tops)

**Rice:** bring the water to a full boil in a covered saucepan. Stir in the rice, making sure none sticks to the bottom. Return to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to very low, and cook 20 minutes. Spread in a large bowl to cool.
Scramble the eggs in 1 Tbsp of the butter. Chop into pea-size pieces with the spatula.
When the rice has cooled, gently toss in the eggs and the peas and carrots.
Melt the remaining 2 Tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the rice mixture.
Stir the soy sauce and sesame oil together and sprinkle evenly over the rice.
Season with white pepper and salt, and garnish with green onion. Serve warm.

notes: Kindra calls it the best fried rice ever.

recipes.title: Tortellini Soup

items: 1 can Italian stewed tomatoes, chopped or blended
In a large pot, brown the sausage.
Add the onion and carrots and cook 3 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Add the broth, tomatoes, and tomato sauce and bring to a boil.
Add the tortellini and heat through.
Just before serving, stir in the spinach until wilted.
Top each bowl with Parmesan, basil, and provolone or mozzarella.

tips: To cook uncooked tortellini right in the soup, increase the broth to 6 cups and boil for the time on the package.

recipes.title: Grandma's Sugared Popcorn

items: Air-pop the popcorn and pick out all the unpopped kernels. Put it in a large bowl and lay out wax paper.
In a saucepan, combine the sugar, cream, corn syrup, and salt. Cook over medium-high heat to the soft-ball stage (235–240°F).
Remove from the heat and stir in food coloring and flavoring, if using.
Pour over the popcorn and stir to coat evenly.
Spread on the wax paper to cool, then break apart.

notes: Bags of this were handed out as favors at Mark and Contessa's wedding reception.

recipes.title: Sesame Chew Bread

items: Preheat the oven to 375°F and grease a large rimmed baking sheet.
Mix the warm water, sugar, salt, yeast, and flour. Don't knead.
Press the dough out to fill the baking sheet.
Pour the melted butter over the top and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake 30 minutes. Tear into pieces and serve warm.

tips: Great with Corn Chowder or Hamburger Soup.
notes: A family favorite. Chase made it to go with dinner.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Fries

items: Put two rimmed baking sheets in the oven and preheat to 425°F.
Peel the potatoes and cut into even 1/4- to 1/2-inch strips or wedges.
Toss with the olive oil in a bowl or zip-top bag, then add the seasonings and toss until evenly coated.
Carefully take out the hot pans. Spread the fries on them so they don't touch, leaving any extra oil behind in the bowl.
Bake 12–15 minutes, flipping halfway if you like, until tender and browned. Serve right away.

tips: These come out tender, not crispy like fast-food fries.
The sugar helps the edges caramelize, but Julie leaves it out and they're just as good.
Julie cuts the salt to 1 tsp, which is plenty for her family.
Make more than you think you need.
notes: Doug found this recipe, and the family made it 4–5 times a week for a while.
Recipe from Mel's Kitchen Cafe.

recipes.title: Rolo Cookies

items: 1 cup sugar, plus more for rolling
Preheat the oven to 375°F. Unwrap the Rolos.
Cream the sugars and butter. Beat in the vanilla and eggs.
In another bowl, whisk the flour, cocoa, and baking soda, then mix into the butter mixture.
Scoop 1 1/2-inch balls of dough. Press a Rolo into the center of each and wrap the dough completely around it.
Roll into a smooth ball, roll in sugar, and set on the cookie sheet. Press the tops lightly with the bottom of a cup so they bake evenly.
Bake 7 minutes. Leave on the sheet 3–5 minutes, then move to a rack.

tips: Best warm, but good anytime.
Make sure the Rolo is fully enclosed. That's what creates the gooey caramel center.
notes: Recipe from Maura Leavitt.

recipes.title: Rolo Pretzel Turtles

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a cookie sheet with foil or parchment.
Lay out the pretzels and top each with an unwrapped Rolo.
Bake 3–4 minutes, until the Rolos look shiny but still hold their shape.
Press a pecan or M&M onto each one. Let firm up about 5 minutes.

notes: Easy enough for kids to make. Julie's family made them as dessert for the missionaries and for a card night with friends.
Recipe from The Sister's Cafe.

recipes.title: Cranberry-Jalapeño Cream Cheese Dip

items: 1 jalapeño pepper, seeded and finely diced
1 cup sugar (more or less to taste)
2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice (about 1 large lemon)
2 (8 oz) packages cream cheese, light or regular, softened
Pulse the cranberries in a food processor until coarsely chopped.
Add the green onions, cilantro, jalapeño, sugar, cumin, lemon juice, and salt and pulse until finely chopped and well combined.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight to mellow the tartness.
To serve, spread the cream cheese evenly on a platter or 9-inch pie plate and top with the cranberry mixture.
Chill up to an hour, then serve with crackers or tortilla chips.

notes: It sounds like an odd combination, but Doug was won over at first bite and wanted to keep it all at home instead of taking it to the party. It was a huge hit there.
Recipe from Mel's Kitchen Cafe.

recipes.title: Cream Cheese Pound Cake

items: Preheat the oven to 300°F. Grease and flour a 10-inch Bundt pan.
