Beat the butter and cream cheese on medium just until creamy (don't overbeat).
Add the eggs one at a time, beating just until combined. Crack them into a separate bowl first to catch any shell.
Sift the flour and mix it with the salt. Add it gradually on low speed, mixing just until blended each time. Stir in the vanilla.
Spread the batter in the pan and smooth the top.
Bake 1 hour 40 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan on a rack 10–15 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.

notes: Ashley found this on Pinterest and calls it simple, moist, and perfect, without a strong cheesecake flavor.
Recipe from *Southern Living*, November 2001.

recipes.title: Garlic Sirloin Kabobs

items: Preheat the grill. If using wooden skewers, soak them first.
Melt the butter and stir in the garlic, garlic salt, and salt.
Cut the steak into 1 1/2-inch cubes. Toss with some of the garlic butter (a zip-top bag works well), saving the rest for basting.
Grill about 15 minutes, turning every couple of minutes and basting often with more garlic butter.
For medium-well, cook to 150°F, or until the center is light pink.

tips: The garlic butter works on whole steaks too.
notes: Kindra says to add this to your summer grilling list.

recipes.title: Stuffed Bell Peppers

items: 6 bell peppers (any color), stems and seeds removed, halved lengthwise
1/4 lb pancetta or lightly smoked bacon, diced
Cook the rice (on the stove or in a rice cooker).
Heat 1 Tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the carrots and celery until tender.
Add the beef and pancetta and cook until browned and crumbled. Drain the fat.
Stir in the marinara, wine, and red pepper flakes and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the cream, half the Parmesan, and the rice. Simmer about 5 minutes more, until most of the liquid is absorbed.
Arrange the pepper halves in a shallow baking dish and fill with the meat mixture. Drizzle with the remaining 1 Tbsp oil and sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan.

tips: Ashley used ground turkey, turkey bacon, and apple juice in place of the wine, and it was great.
Cut the peppers into pieces after baking to make them easier to eat.
notes: Ashley found this recipe as a way to use up a pile of bell peppers.

recipes.title: Mrs. Fields Chocolate Chip Cookies

items: Whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt in a bowl and set aside.
Cream the brown sugar, sugar, and butter. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Mix in the flour mixture, then the chocolate chips (and nuts, if using).
Drop onto baking sheets and bake 22–24 minutes.

tips: **Oatmeal version:** swap some oats for an equal amount of flour. Blake's sister Tyre recommends 1/2 cup. Some people blend the oats first.
notes: The Russell family's go-to recipe for as long as Blake can remember.

recipes.title: Cafe Rio Barbacoa Pork (with Black Beans, Cilantro-Lime Rice, and Dressing)

ingredients.heading: Pork
items: 3/4 (10 oz) can Old El Paso red enchilada sauce

ingredients.heading: Cilantro ranch dressing (makes 1 quart)
items: 1 package (3 Tbsp) Hidden Valley Ranch dressing mix (traditional, not buttermilk)

steps.heading: Pork (about 5 hours, plus marinating)
items: Put the pork, 1 1/2 cans Coke, and 1/4 cup brown sugar in a zip-top bag. Marinate a few hours or overnight.
Drain the pork and put it in the slow cooker with 1/2 can Coke, the water, and the garlic salt. Cook on high 3–4 hours, until it shreds easily.
In a blender, blend 1/2 can Coke, the green chiles, the enchilada sauce, and 1 cup brown sugar.
Drain the pork again and shred it. Return it to the slow cooker with the blended sauce and cook 1 hour more.

steps.heading: Black beans
items: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium. Add the garlic and cumin and cook until fragrant.
Add the beans, salt, and tomato juice and bring to a boil. Simmer on medium-low 20 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro before serving.

steps.heading: Cilantro-lime rice
items: Melt the butter in a saucepan with the garlic. Add the rice, 1 tsp lime juice, and the broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook 15–20 minutes.
Mix the sugar, cilantro, and 1 Tbsp lime juice, then stir it into the cooked rice and fluff.

steps.heading: Dressing
items: Blend everything until smooth. Refrigerate, ideally overnight.

steps.heading: Serve
items: Build burritos or salads with tortillas, beans, rice, pork, cheese, and dressing. Add pico de gallo, guacamole, sour cream, lettuce, tortilla strips, or cotija if you like.

tips: **Which pork?** Boneless ribs and almost any roast (picnic, sirloin, rump, shoulder) work. If it won't shred, it just needs more time. Cut roasts into baseball-size chunks to speed things up.
Brittany triples the pork, beans, and rice for leftovers. One batch of dressing is plenty.
Uncooked grocery-store tortillas (near the cheese) are excellent.
If the jalapeño seeds make the dressing too spicy, leave them out.
**Julie's rice method:** boil the broth, add the rice, return to a boil, then cover and cook on low 20 minutes. Stir in the garlic, sugar, cilantro, and lime juice at the end.
notes: Brittany's favorite meal. She'll happily eat it three times a day.
Adapted slightly from Favorite Family Recipes.

recipes.title: Naan

items: In a small bowl, stir together the sugar, warm water, and yeast. Let stand about 10 minutes, until foamy.
In a stand mixer, combine the flour and salt. Add the yeast mixture, yogurt, and oil and knead 3–4 minutes, until smooth and shiny.
Cover and let rise until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces and roll each into an 8-inch circle.
Heat a skillet (cast iron is best) over high heat and wipe it lightly with oil.
Cook one naan at a time until it puffs and browns on the bottom, then flip and brown the other side.
Brush with melted butter while hot.

notes: Submitted by Mom in 2011. In 2019 Dad found this new version, the best yet. They had been chasing the naan from their favorite Indian restaurant, Seva.

recipes.title: Mom and Dad's Cinnamon Rolls

steps.heading: Dough
items: Warm the milk to lukewarm. In a large mixing bowl, combine the milk, yeast, sugar, warm water, salt, oil, eggs, and potato flakes.
Stir in 3–4 cups of the flour, then add more a little at a time just until you can knead it. Keep the dough as soft as possible; that's the secret to tender rolls.
Let rest 10 minutes, then knead 10 minutes.
Let rise in a warm place until doubled. Punch down and let rise 30 minutes more.

steps.heading: Shape and bake
items: On a floured surface, roll the dough out fairly thick.
Spread with softened butter, then sprinkle with brown sugar, cinnamon, and a little white sugar.
Roll up tightly and cut into 12–16 rolls. Place in greased pans and let rise until puffy.
Bake at 400°F for 10–12 minutes, until golden and cooked through.

steps.heading: Frosting
items: Beat powdered sugar with the margarine and vanilla, adding milk a little at a time until spreadable. Frost the warm rolls.

tips: **Orange rolls:** spread the dough with soft butter and sprinkle with white sugar mixed with grated orange peel instead of the cinnamon filling. Bake and frost the same way.
This dough also makes great dinner rolls.
notes: Mom and Dad's classic. Julie made these for Douglas' birthday.

recipes.title: Breakfast Burritos with Roasted Tomatoes

items: Salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes
Grated pepper jack or cheddar cheese
Toss the tomatoes and onion with the olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast 15 minutes. Don't skip this step; it's what makes these special.

Meanwhile, whisk the eggs, milk, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes. Cook slowly in a pan over medium heat, stirring. Take them off the heat just before they're done; they'll finish cooking on their own.
Warm each tortilla in a dry skillet for a few seconds per side.
Lay spinach down the middle of each tortilla, then add roasted tomatoes and onion, eggs, cheese, and avocado.
Roll up, or fold like a taco if it's too full to roll.

notes: Julie eats these for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, several times a week.

recipes.title: Ultimate Chicken Fingers

items: 3 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 1 lb), cut crosswise into 1/2-inch strips
Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet with foil and spray with cooking spray.
In a bowl (or a gallon zip-top bag), mix the Bisquick, Parmesan, salt, and paprika.
Dip the chicken strips in egg, then coat well in the Bisquick mixture, pressing it on firmly. Place on the baking sheet.
Bake 12–14 minutes, turning halfway, until no longer pink in the center.

tips: Kindra coats them in a bowl so she can pack on more breading, and mists them with cooking spray instead of butter. The spray stays on better than butter, which tends to run off.
notes: From the back of the Bisquick box, and worth the reminder.

recipes.title: Parmesan Chicken

items: 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan, plus extra for serving

ingredients.heading: Lemon salad (optional)
items: 1/4 cup freshly squeezed lemon juice (2 lemons)
Pound the chicken to an even 1/4-inch thickness with a meat mallet or rolling pin.
Set up three plates: flour mixed with the salt and pepper; eggs beaten with the water; and bread crumbs mixed with the 1/2 cup Parmesan.
Coat each breast in flour, then egg, then the crumb mixture, pressing so it sticks.
Heat 1 Tbsp butter and 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Cook 2–3 breasts at a time, 2–3 minutes per side, until cooked through. Add more butter and oil for each batch.
**For the salad version:** whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss with the greens and pile on top of the hot chicken. Serve with extra Parmesan.

tips: **Ashley's version:** skip the salad. Put the cooked chicken in a pan, cover it with spaghetti sauce and mozzarella, heat until melted, and serve over pasta. The sauce softens the crust, so skip this if you want it crispy.
Dip twice through the egg and crumbs for a thicker, crunchier crust.
If the chicken is thicker than 1/4 inch, finish it in the oven so the outside doesn't burn.
Regular salt and canola oil work fine.
notes: Adapted from Ina Garten.

recipes.title: Simply Delicious Strawberry Cake

ingredients.heading: Strawberry cream cheese frosting
items: 1 (10 oz) package frozen strawberries in syrup, thawed and puréed
Preheat the oven to 350°F and lightly grease two 9-inch round pans.
Purée the thawed strawberries. Set aside 1/4 cup for the frosting; the rest goes in the cake.
Combine the cake mix and gelatin. Add the strawberry purée, eggs, oil, and water and beat on medium until smooth.
Divide between the pans and bake about 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then turn out and cool completely on racks.
**Frosting:** beat the butter and cream cheese until creamy. Beat in the reserved 1/4 cup purée and the strawberry extract, then gradually add the confectioners' sugar until smooth.
Frost between the layers and over the top and sides. Garnish with fresh strawberries if you like.

tips: Any extra purée is great in smoothies or over ice cream.
notes: One of Kindra's Paula Deen favorites. It tastes like summer.

recipes.title: Wedding Cookies

items: 1/2 cup powdered sugar, plus more for rolling
In a large bowl, mix the butter, 1/2 cup powdered sugar, and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, nuts, and salt until the dough holds together.
Roll into 1-inch balls and place about 1 inch apart on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 10–12 minutes, until set but not browned.
Let cool slightly, then roll the warm cookies in powdered sugar. Cool completely on a rack and roll in powdered sugar again.

notes: Buttery, powdery, melt-in-your-mouth. The last cookie Julie adds to her Christmas plates.

recipes.title: Dreamy Chocolate Mousse Cake

ingredients.heading: Assembly
items: 2 boxes chocolate cake mix, baked as directed (or the chocolate cake below)
Grated chocolate and chocolate curls, for garnish

steps.heading: Mousse (make first; it chills 4 hours)
items: Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water and let stand 2 minutes. Stir in the boiling water until dissolved. Set aside.
Mix the powdered sugar and cocoa.
Beat the cream on medium until foamy. Gradually add the cocoa mixture and beat to stiff peaks. Stir in the gelatin.

steps.heading: Cake
items: **From a box:** bake both mixes according to the package as four 9-inch layers.

**From scratch:** preheat the oven to 350°F and grease and flour three 9-inch pans. Combine the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder, and baking soda. Add the milk, coffee, oil, and eggs and beat on medium until smooth. Divide among the pans and bake 23–25 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then turn out onto racks and cool completely.

steps.heading: Frosting
items: In a saucepan, bring the sugar and cream to a boil over medium-high heat. Lower the heat and simmer 6 minutes, stirring often.
Remove from the heat and stir in the chocolate and butter until smooth. Cool 10 minutes.
Whisk in the confectioners' sugar and let cool until spreadable.

steps.heading: Assemble
items: With a serrated knife, split the cake layers in half horizontally. Choose the 6 best layers.
Set one layer cut-side up on a cake plate and spread with one-fifth of the mousse. Repeat, ending with a plain cake layer on top.
Spread the frosting over the top and sides. Press grated chocolate onto the sides and top with chocolate curls.

tips: With box mix you'll get 8 layers after splitting. Use the best 6 and snack on the rest.
notes: Updated by Kindra in November 2020 to make it easier.

recipes.title: Peanut Blossoms

items: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Unwrap the Kisses.
Cream the butter, peanut butter, and both sugars. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the flour, baking soda, and salt.
Roll into balls and place on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake 8 minutes. Gently press a Kiss into the center of each cookie and bake 3 minutes more. Don't overbake.

notes: A Christmas-plate favorite.
Recipe from Sister's Cafe.

recipes.title: Peppermint Bark

items: Spray a 10x15-inch rimmed baking sheet with nonstick spray and line it with wax or parchment paper.
Melt the white chocolate in the microwave: 1 minute on high, stir, then 30-second bursts, stirring each time, until smooth.
Stir in the rice cereal and peppermint oil.
Spread evenly to the edges of the pan.
Sprinkle with the crushed candy canes. Lay a sheet of wax paper over the top and press gently so the candy sticks.
Chill 20–30 minutes, until firm (no longer, or the candy starts to soften).
Peel off the paper and break into pieces. Store airtight at room temperature for up to 1 week.

tips: White chocolate chips work fine, even though the original recipe says not to use them.
Starlight mints work too, but they're much harder to crush.
Swap crushed Oreos for the peppermint to make cookies-and-cream bark.
notes: Julie posted this for Ashley. Doug isn't a mint-dessert fan (he says it tastes like toothpaste), but the kids loved it.
Based on a Martha Stewart recipe.

recipes.title: Seasoned Pretzels

items: Put the pretzels in a large bowl.
Whisk the oil, garlic powder, cayenne, and ranch mix, pour over the pretzels, and stir until evenly coated.
Spread on a rimmed baking sheet and bake 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
Cool and store in an airtight container.

notes: Easy and a little zesty. Good for parties or after-school snacks.

recipes.title: Almond Joys or Mounds (Chocolate-Covered Coconut Bars)

items: Line a baking sheet with wax or parchment paper.
With a mixer, combine the coconut, powdered sugar, butter, and corn syrup.
Divide into 15 portions and press each into a firm 2-inch bar. Top with an almond for Almond Joys. Refrigerate 10 minutes.
Melt the chocolate. Dip the bars one at a time and return them to the paper.
Let stand about 30 minutes, until the chocolate is firm.

recipes.title: Breakfast Pizza

items: 1 (8 oz) can reduced-fat refrigerated crescent roll dough
12 oz turkey breakfast sausage, regular sausage, or bacon
1 cup frozen shredded hash brown potatoes, thawed
1 cup (4 oz) shredded fat-free cheddar cheese
Preheat the oven to 375°F and spray a 12-inch pizza pan.
Unroll the crescent dough, separate the triangles, and press them together into one round crust. Pinch the edge up to form a rim.
Optional but recommended: prebake the crust about 7 minutes.
Cook the sausage (or bacon) in a skillet over medium heat until browned, crumbling as it cooks. Drain.
Scatter the meat, hash browns, and cheddar over the crust.
Whisk the milk, salt, pepper, and eggs, and carefully pour over the toppings. Sprinkle with Parmesan.
Bake 25 minutes, until the crust is browned and the eggs are set.

tips: Do half bacon and half sausage to please everyone.
Reheats well.

recipes.title: Pizza Rolls

items: Frozen roll dough or homemade pizza dough
Pizza toppings of choice, diced small (such as pepperoni cut in quarters, green pepper)
Olive oil, garlic salt, and Italian seasoning, for the tops
Let frozen rolls thaw about 1 hour, until soft but still cold.
Preheat the oven to 400°F and lightly grease a baking dish.
Flatten each roll. Smear a little pizza sauce in the center, keeping the edges clean so they'll seal.
Add cheese and any small toppings, then press a few pepperoni pieces on top to hold everything in place.
Wrap the dough around the filling and pinch firmly to seal. Fewer toppings are easier to wrap.
Place seam-side down in the dish. Brush with olive oil and sprinkle generously with garlic salt and Italian seasoning.
Bake 12–15 minutes, until light golden. Watch closely.
Serve with warm marinara for dipping.

notes: A fun pizza-night twist, good for kids and for anyone who doesn't like pizza sauce. Julie's family does pepperoni and cheese, plain cheese, and pepperoni with green pepper.
Recipe from Sister's Cafe.

recipes.title: No-Bake Cookies

items: Lay out foil, wax paper, or parchment.
In a saucepan, bring the sugar, milk, cocoa, and butter to a boil and simmer for 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the peanut butter and vanilla.
Stir in the oats until it's as thick as you like (about 4 cups).
Drop by spoonfuls onto the paper and let cool slightly.

notes: The way Dad and Slade make them, so now everyone can have good no-bakes anytime.

recipes.title: Comfort Corn Pudding

items: Mix everything together in a large bowl until blended.
Pour into a shallow 2-quart baking dish.

tips: Goes with almost anything: burgers, hot dogs, grilled chicken, barbecue sandwiches, roast, or pulled pork.
notes: Recipe from A. Trzeciak. Julie says it takes about five minutes to throw together and always gets rave reviews.

recipes.title: Buttercream Icing

items: 1/2 cup (1 stick) butter or margarine, softened
Beat the shortening, butter, and vanilla until creamy.
Gradually beat in the confectioners' sugar.
Add milk or water a little at a time until the icing reaches the consistency you want. You may not need all of it.

tips: The rule of thumb is 1 cup fat to 1 lb sugar. All butter tastes great but is more yellow; all shortening isn't as tasty. Kindra likes the half-and-half mix.
Swap the vanilla for almond or butter flavoring.

recipes.title: Crash Hot Potatoes

items: 12 whole new potatoes (or other small round potatoes)
Boil the potatoes in salted water until fork-tender.
Drizzle a sheet pan generously with olive oil and spread the potatoes out with plenty of space between them.
Press each potato with a potato masher until it flattens a bit, then turn the masher 90 degrees and press again.
Brush the tops generously with more olive oil and sprinkle with salt, pepper, and chopped herbs.
Bake 20–25 minutes, until golden and crispy.

tips: Smaller potatoes give you more crispy edges. Yukon gold and small red potatoes both work well.
Rosemary, chives, thyme, or green onion all work as the herb.
Plan on at least two per adult.
notes: A big hit in Julie's house, even with people who aren't huge potato fans.
Recipe from The Pioneer Woman.

recipes.title: Double Broccoli Quinoa

items: 5 cups raw broccoli, cut into small florets and stems
2/3 cup sliced or slivered almonds, toasted

**Chile oil (ideally a day ahead):** warm the olive oil in a small pan for a couple of minutes, to sautéing temperature but not smoking. Turn off the heat, stir in the pepper flakes, cool, and refrigerate. Bring back to room temperature before using.
Cook the quinoa according to the package.

Bring 3/4 cup water to a simmer in a large pot with a pinch of salt. Add the broccoli, cover, and cook about 1 minute, just to take the raw edge off. Drain and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking.

For the broccoli pesto, put 2 cups of the broccoli, the garlic, 1/2 cup of the almonds, the Parmesan, a pinch of salt, and the lemon juice in a food processor. With it running, drizzle in the olive oil and cream and blend until smooth.
Just before serving, toss the quinoa and remaining broccoli with about half the pesto. Taste and add more pesto, salt, or lemon as needed.
Pile onto a platter and top with the remaining almonds, a drizzle of chile oil, avocado, and any other toppings.

tips: Quinoa cooks fine in a rice cooker using the same 2:1 water ratio as rice.
notes: Adapted from 101 Cookbooks. Julie calls it light, healthy, and full of good stuff.

recipes.title: Beef Stroganoff

items: 1 Tbsp Kitchen Bouquet (or 1 packet brown gravy mix)
Cut the steak into bite-size pieces (stew beef works perfectly).
In a bowl or large plastic bag, mix the flour, salt, and pepper. Add the beef and toss to coat.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and brown the beef. Stir in any leftover flour mixture, then remove from the heat.
Transfer the beef to a casserole dish and stir in the broth and Kitchen Bouquet. Bake 1 1/2 hours.
Meanwhile, cook rice or noodles. Slice the mushrooms and onion and sauté each in butter until golden.
When the stroganoff comes out of the oven, stir in the sour cream. Temper it first (stir in a little hot sauce before adding it) if you're worried about clumps.
If it's thinner than you'd like, whisk in a little more flour. It thickens as it cools.
Serve over rice or noodles, topped with mushrooms and onions.

tips: **Slow cooker:** brown the beef, then add everything except the sour cream. Cook on high 4 hours or low 6 hours. Stir in the sour cream just before serving.
Corn is a great side.
notes: Blake's favorite, always with mushrooms.
Recipe by Kerry and Jeanne Thackeray.

recipes.title: Hamburger Soup

items: In a stockpot, cook the ground beef and onion until the beef is browned.
Add the water, carrots, celery, potatoes, salt, pepper, bouillon, sugar, oregano, and bay leaf.
Simmer about 30 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and stir in the blended tomatoes and tomato sauce. Heat through.

tips: **Slow cooker:** brown the beef and onion, then put everything in the slow cooker with the raw vegetables and cook on high 8–10 hours.
Or cook it on the stove and keep it warm in the slow cooker until serving.
notes: Recipe by Jeanne Thackeray. Julie asked for this with bread for her birthday dinner every year as a kid.

recipes.title: Josie H's Chocolate Chip Cookies

items: Cream the shortening with both sugars. Beat in the eggs, vanilla, and water until well combined.
Add 3 cups of the flour, the salt, and the baking soda, then the remaining 1/2 cup flour. Mix until almost combined.
Add the chocolate chips and M&M's and mix just until combined.
Scoop with a small cookie scoop (or drop by spoonfuls) onto baking sheets.
Bake about 9 minutes, just until they barely start to brown. Don't overbake.

tips: Mix up the add-ins: half peanut butter chips, mint chips, extra-large chips, just chocolate chips, or regular M&M's pressed on top after baking.
notes: Brittany's friend Josie made these one late night in high school, and they've been a favorite ever since. In Brittany's house they're called "chocolate chip treats" to set them apart from every other cookie.
Recipe by Josie H.

recipes.title: Chicken and Broccoli Bake

items: 3 (10 oz) packages frozen broccoli, or 5–6 fresh bunches
Simmer the chicken in water until cooked through. Let cool, then pull into golf-ball-size pieces.
Spread the broccoli in a 9x13-inch pan and lay the chicken on top.
In a saucepan, heat the soup, milk, mayonnaise, and Miracle Whip, stirring until smooth. Remove from the heat and stir in the cheddar and lemon juice.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and broccoli and sprinkle with Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake 1 hour, removing the foil for the last 30 minutes.

tips: **Julie's shortcut:** skip simmering the chicken. Cut raw chicken into golf-ball-size pieces and lay them on fresh broccoli. Whisk the sauce in a bowl instead of heating it. Bake the same way, but leave the foil on until the last 10 minutes or so. The chicken comes out very tender.
Fresh broccoli cooks down a lot, so pack in as much as will fit.
notes: Recipe by Sharon Lyons. Julie's family has asked for it again.

recipes.title: Aunt Renee's Chicken Stir-Fry

items: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces
Heat the oil in a large skillet. Mince the garlic and add it with the chicken and minced onion. Cook until the chicken is done.
Add the frozen broccoli and 1 cup of the broth. Cover and simmer until the broccoli is as tender as you like.
In a 2-cup measuring cup, stir the brown sugar, soy sauce, fruit juice, and cornstarch with a fork until smooth.
Stir the sauce again right before adding it (the cornstarch settles), then pour it into the skillet and stir as it heats and thickens.
If it gets too thick, thin it with some of the remaining broth.
Serve over rice, sprinkled with peanuts.

tips: Use whatever stir-fry vegetables your family likes: fresh, frozen, or a California blend. The original recipe used blanched sliced carrots and green peppers.
Swap cashews for the peanuts to make cashew chicken.
Serve with fried rice, egg rolls, or crab rangoon for a takeout-style night.
notes: A family staple. Julie adapted it from Aunt Renee T.'s recipe in the ward cookbook.

recipes.title: Pomegranate Cheesecake

steps.heading: Crust
items: Beat the butter 30 seconds, then beat in the brown sugar, the egg, and finally the flour. Divide the dough in half; cover and chill one half.
Take the ring off a 10-inch springform pan. Press the other half of the dough over the base, almost to the edge. Set the base on a baking sheet and bake 10 minutes. Cool completely.
Reattach the ring. Press the chilled dough 1 3/4 inches up the inside of the ring, using an offset spatula to smooth it.

steps.heading: Filling
items: In a large bowl, beat the cream cheese and sugar until fluffy. Beat in the flour on low until smooth.
Add the eggs and vanilla and beat on low just until combined. Mix in the sour cream and lemon peel.
With a spatula (not the mixer, which would burst them and stain the filling), gently fold in the 3/4 cup pomegranate seeds.
Pour into the crust, set the pan on a baking sheet, and bake about 65 minutes, until the edges puff and the center jiggles slightly. A crack on top is fine.

steps.heading: Topping
items: Stir together the sour cream, sugar, and vanilla and spread gently over the hot cheesecake. Bake 10 minutes more.
Cool on a rack 15 minutes, run a knife around the edge, and cool 30 minutes more. Remove the ring and cool completely.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.

steps.heading: Glaze
items: Boil the pomegranate juice in a saucepan, uncovered, until reduced to 1 cup (12–15 minutes).
Stir the brown sugar and cornstarch together, add to the juice, and cook and stir until thick and bubbly. Cook 2 minutes more.
Pour into a bowl, press plastic wrap onto the surface, cool, and refrigerate.

steps.heading: Serve
items: Take the cheesecake and glaze out of the fridge 15 minutes before serving.
Spoon some glaze over the top and pile the 1/2 cup pomegranate seeds in the center. Pass the remaining glaze at the table.

tips: Reduced-fat sour cream works well in both the filling and topping.
Look for pomegranate juice in the refrigerated juice section.
notes: Recipe from My Kitchen Cafe.

recipes.title: Rainbow Jello

items: Make sure your fridge shelf is level, or the layers will set in wedges.
**Creamy layer:** dissolve 1 package purple Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water. Whisk in 1/3 cup sour cream until smooth. Pour into a 9x13-inch pan and refrigerate until set, about 1 hour.
**Clear layer:** dissolve the second package purple Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water and stir in 3 Tbsp cold water. Pour slowly over the set creamy layer and refrigerate until set, about 1 hour.
Repeat both layers with each color: blue, green, yellow, orange, then red, so the finished dish reads red-orange-yellow-green-blue-purple from the top down.

tips: Pour each warm layer slowly and spread it around rather than in one spot, so it doesn't break through the layer below.
For a sharp look, skim off the air bubbles on each layer (or at least the top two).
A standard 9x13 fits about 10 layers; a 9.5x13.5 or 10x14 pan fits all 12.
Use flavors you like and any colors in any order. Strawberry makes the prettiest red top. Peach doesn't give a true orange.
Spread the work over 2 days if you can. The longer each layer sets, the better, and it saves you from being stuck by the stove all day.
notes: From Brittany and Julie. A holiday favorite.

recipes.title: Green Chicken Chili

items: 1 1/4 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast halves
4 large handfuls tortilla chips, plus more for serving
1 (15 oz) can small red beans, drained

In a deep skillet, bring the broth and chicken to a simmer over medium heat. Lower the heat slightly and poach, turning occasionally, about 10 minutes, until just cooked through. Move the chicken to a plate to cool, keeping the broth.
Crumble the 4 handfuls of chips into a food processor, pour in 3 cups of the hot broth, and let them soften. Save the remaining 1 cup broth.
In a large saucepan, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the scallions, oregano, and cumin and cook about 2 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the reserved 1 cup broth, the beans, and the salsa and bring to a simmer.
Purée the chips and broth until smooth, then whisk into the pot.
Shred the chicken, add it to the chili, and heat through over medium-low, stirring.

tips: The heat level depends on your salsa. Top bowls with pepper jack for extra kick.
For bite-size chunks instead of shredded chicken, cube raw chicken and brown it in a little olive oil, or use leftover cooked chicken.
notes: Julie has entered this in her ward chili cook-off several years running. It hasn't won, but it always gets compliments.
Recipe by Rachael Ray.

recipes.title: Lemon Cream Pasta

items: 3 cups shredded or cubed Lemon Garlic Chicken
1 (16 oz) package tube pasta, such as penne
In a large saucepan, season the chicken broth with the garlic powder and pepper and bring to a boil.
Add the lemon juice and the uncooked pasta. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has absorbed all the liquid, about 25 minutes. It sounds unusual, but it works.
Stir in the chicken, cream, Parmesan, and lemon zest. Cook over low heat, stirring, for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand 5 minutes. Stir well before serving.

tips: Leftover Lemon and Garlic Grilled Chicken makes this come together fast.
notes: Recipe from My Kitchen Cafe.

recipes.title: Bread Bowls

items: In a large mixing bowl, dissolve the yeast in the warm water. Let stand about 10 minutes, until creamy.
Add the salt, oil, and 4 cups of the flour and beat well.
Add the remaining flour 1/2 cup at a time, beating on medium after each addition, until the dough is soft but not sticky. You may not need all 7 cups.
Knead on a lightly floured surface (or in the mixer) about 6 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Place in an oiled bowl, turn to coat, cover with a damp cloth, and let rise in a warm place about 40 minutes, until doubled.
Punch down and divide into 6–8 equal pieces. Shape each into a smooth ball.
Place on baking sheets sprinkled with cornmeal (or lined with parchment or silicone mats), spaced so they don't touch each other or the pan sides. Cover and let rise about 35 minutes, until doubled.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Beat the egg white with 1 Tbsp water.
Brush the loaves on all exposed sides with half the egg wash. Bake 15 minutes.
Brush with the remaining egg wash and bake 10–15 minutes more, until golden. Cool on racks.
To serve, cut a circle in the top of each bowl and pull out the inside bread, leaving a thick wall. Fill with soup.

tips: The egg wash is what makes the crust sturdy enough to hold soup, so coat every side that isn't touching the pan.
If a spot looks thin, leave more bread inside there to prevent leaks.
Creamy soups and thick chilis work best.
Make smaller bowls for kids, and turn leftover dough into crusty rolls (same method, smaller size, still egg-washed).
Serve the pulled-out bread and the tops alongside for dipping.
notes: Julie suggests these for an impressive dinner for family or company. They're not hard to make.
Recipe from My Kitchen Cafe (Italian Bread Bowls). Julie recommends filling them with that site's broccoli cheese soup or chicken and wild rice soup.

recipes.title: Martha Stewart's Banana Bread

items: 2 cups very ripe bananas, mashed (about 3 bananas)
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease two 9x5x3-inch loaf pans.
With a mixer, cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing each in fully and scraping down the bowl as needed.
In another bowl, whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt. Add to the butter mixture and mix just until combined.
By hand, stir in the bananas, sour cream, and vanilla just until combined. Fold in the nuts, if using.
Divide between the pans and bake about 1 hour (sometimes up to 1 hour 10 minutes), until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.

tips: Baking time depends on your pans (glass, metal, dark, wide, or narrow). Start checking early, since overbaked banana bread is dry.
Mashing the bananas with the mixer ahead of time makes this quicker.
notes: After a long search for a good banana bread, Brittany found this one wonderfully moist.
Recipe by Martha Stewart.

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Chicken

items: Cut the chicken into chunks and season with salt and pepper.
Dip the pieces in cornstarch, then in egg.
Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the chicken until browned but not cooked through. Arrange in a single layer in a baking dish.
Whisk the sauce ingredients together and pour over the chicken.
Bake 1 hour, turning the chicken every 15 minutes.

tips: **Extra sauce:** simmer a second batch of sauce on the stove over medium heat, stirring, for 6–8 minutes until thickened.
If you like buffalo sauce, try the Buffalo Chicken Bites variation.
notes: Julie found this on My Kitchen Cafe, and it was a hit at both her house and Brittany's. You'll almost always have the ingredients on hand.

recipes.title: Buffalo Chicken Bites

items: Cut the chicken into bite-size chunks and season with salt and pepper.
Dip each piece in cornstarch, then in the beaten egg.
Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the chicken until browned. You can cook it all the way through here, or just brown it and finish it in the oven.
If baking: arrange in a single layer in a baking dish and bake 1 hour, turning every 15 minutes.
Warm the hot sauce and butter together (the microwave works fine) and toss with the cooked chicken.

tips: Want more sauce? Make a second batch to drizzle over the top.
More butter makes it milder; less butter makes it spicier.
notes: Julie came up with this spin on the family-favorite Sweet and Sour Chicken.

recipes.title: Baked Ziti

items: 1 lb ziti noodles, cooked and drained
1 lb ground beef, cooked and drained
Toss the cooked ziti with 1 cup of the spaghetti sauce.
In a separate bowl, mix the ricotta, parsley, Parmesan, egg, salt, and pepper.
Spread 1/3–1/2 cup sauce in the bottom of a 2-quart baking dish.
Layer half the ziti, half the ricotta mixture (in dollops), half the beef, half the remaining sauce, and 1 cup mozzarella.
Repeat with the rest of the ziti, ricotta, beef, and sauce. Top with the last 1 cup mozzarella.
Cover with foil (spray the underside with cooking spray so it doesn't stick to the cheese) and bake 45 minutes.

tips: This feeds a crowd. For a smaller family, halve everything and bake it in a 9x9-inch dish.

recipes.title: Pesto Pizza with Pine Nuts and Feta

items: If using a pizza stone, put it in the cold oven, then preheat the oven to 475°F and let the stone heat for about 30 minutes. This gives a crisp, restaurant-style crust.
Roll out the dough and set it on a floured pizza peel (or a pizza pan if you're not using a stone).
Spread a thin layer of pesto all the way to the edges. Too much makes it greasy.
Add the chicken, feta, onion, tomatoes, mozzarella, and pine nuts. Save a few toppings to scatter over the final layer of cheese.
Slide onto the hot stone and bake 8–10 minutes, until nicely browned.

tips: The Pizza Hut Pizza Dough recipe works well here.
Halved grape tomatoes are a good stand-in for sliced tomatoes.
notes: Recipe from My Kitchen Cafe.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies

items: In a large bowl, beat the sugar, brown sugar, peanut butter, butter, eggs, and vanilla until combined.
Stir in the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt, then the chocolate chips.
Roll the dough into balls and place on a baking sheet. Dip a fork in sugar and press a criss-cross pattern into each one.
Bake about 8 minutes, until lightly browned at the edges but still pale in the middle. Don't overbake.

tips: You can chill the dough for 2 hours before baking, but Julie skips this and they still turn out great.
Semi-sweet chips work, and they're good peanut butter cookies without any chips at all.
notes: Julie's favorite cookie, and nearly foolproof as long as you don't overbake them.
Adapted from *Betty Crocker's New Cookbook*.

Trim the ends off the green beans and rinse them.
Bring a large pot of water to a hard boil. Add the beans, wait just until the water returns to a boil (5–30 seconds), and drain them in a colander.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Carefully add the beans and garlic and stir-fry about 3 minutes for crisp-tender, or longer if you like them softer.
Add the soy sauce and stir-fry 1 minute. Add the sugar and stir-fry 30 seconds more. Season with black pepper.

recipes.title: Blake and Kindra's Salsa

items: 1 (28 oz) can diced tomatoes (the cheaper brand is best)
1 Tbsp minced garlic or 2–3 cloves, diced
Stir everything together in a bowl, starting with 1 jalapeño. Taste and add more jalapeño if you want more heat.

tips: Use less sugar if you add diced carrots.
There are no preservatives, so eat it within a few days.

recipes.title: Berry Trifle

items: 2 small packages white chocolate instant pudding mix
1 prepared angel food cake, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 carton (8 oz) frozen whipped topping, thawed
Whisk the pudding mix and cold milk for about 2 minutes, until thickened.
In a trifle bowl or large glass bowl, layer one-third of the cake cubes, then one-third of the pudding.
Add 1 cup sliced strawberries, placing some against the glass so they show. Add one-third of the raspberries and one-third of the blueberries, then one-third of the whipped topping.
Repeat the layers two more times.
Top with the quartered strawberries. Cover and refrigerate until serving.

notes: Julie's mother-in-law, Karen, makes this one. Perfect for summer.
Adapted slightly from Taste of Home.

recipes.title: Fruit Pizza

ingredients.heading: Crust and filling
items: 2 tubes (8 oz each) refrigerated crescent rolls
1 carton (8 oz) frozen whipped topping, thawed
Preheat the oven to 375°F and grease a rimmed cookie sheet.
Unroll the crescent dough onto the pan and press it over the bottom and up the sides, pinching the seams closed.
Bake 15–20 minutes, until golden brown. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Beat the cream cheese, confectioners' sugar, and jam until smooth. Fold in the whipped topping and spread over the cooled crust.
Peel and slice the kiwi, then arrange all the fruit over the top.

tips: Blackberry jam works in place of raspberry. Blackberries are a good fruit to add, too.
A sprinkle of coconut on top is a nice touch.
notes: Mom made this for a graduation breakfast, and Ashley calls it the best breakfast, dessert, or anytime food.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Roll Monkey Bread

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a Bundt pan.
Stir together the butter, sour cream, brown sugar, vanilla, nuts, and raisins. Set aside the frosting cups from the cinnamon roll cans.
Cut the cinnamon rolls into quarters and toss them in the butter mixture.
Pour everything into the pan and bake 30–40 minutes, until cooked through.
Turn out onto a plate and spread with the frosting that came with the rolls. Serve warm.

notes: Brittany got this recipe from Julie.

recipes.title: Blueberry Cheesecake Pancakes

items: **Topping:** beat the cream cheese and whipped topping until smooth. Refrigerate until serving.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, graham cracker crumbs, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
In another bowl, whisk the eggs, buttermilk, and melted butter. Stir into the dry ingredients just until moistened. Gently fold in the blueberries.
Pour 1/4 cup of batter at a time onto a greased hot griddle. Flip when bubbles form on top, and cook until the second side is golden.
Spread the topping over the pancakes, drizzle with warm syrup, and sprinkle with extra blueberries if you like.

tips: Frozen blueberries make them cook a little unevenly. Give them a bit more time on the griddle and they turn out fine.
notes: Doug posted this one and joked that he lost his "man card" long ago.
Garrison asked for these for his birthday breakfast.
Adapted from Taste of Home.

recipes.title: Lemon and Garlic Grilled Chicken

items: Trim the chicken and slice thick breasts into thinner, tenderloin-size pieces so they soak up more marinade.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, salt, pepper, and oregano.
Put the chicken in a zip-top bag (or a covered 9x13-inch dish), pour in the marinade, and refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight.
Grill over medium-high heat (or cook in a skillet) until cooked through.

tips: Double the batch and freeze the extra cooked chicken. It's great for salads, Hawaiian haystacks, pizza, pasta, or fettuccine Alfredo.
notes: Julie's favorite grilled chicken. It's flavorful enough that it doesn't need barbecue sauce.
Recipe from My Kitchen Cafe.

recipes.title: Sweet and Spicy Slow Cooker Chicken Tacos

items: 1 (14 oz) can petite diced tomatoes, undrained
1/4 to 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes
Spray the inside of the slow cooker with nonstick spray.
Add the chicken, tomatoes with their juice, brown sugar, and red pepper flakes.
Cook on high for 4–6 hours or on low for 8–10 hours, until the chicken shreds easily.
Shred the chicken with two forks and stir it back into the sauce. It will soak up the liquid as it sits. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve in tortillas with tomatoes, lettuce, cheese, and sour cream.

tips: If your kids don't like tomato chunks, blend the tomatoes first.
Julie used 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes.
notes: Recipe from My Kitchen Cafe.

recipes.title: Crepes with Cream Cheese Filling and Strawberries

steps.heading: Crepes
items: Whisk the flour, salt, and sugar. Add 1 cup of the milk and whisk until smooth.
Beat in the eggs one at a time. Add the oil and vanilla and mix well, then whisk in the remaining 1 cup milk.
Heat a skillet or crepe pan over medium heat and spray with cooking spray.
Pour in a thin layer of batter and swirl to coat the pan. Cook until the top looks dry, then flip briefly or slide out.

steps.heading: Filling
items: Beat the cream cheese until smooth. Add the cottage cheese and beat again.
Fold in the Cool Whip and powdered sugar.

steps.heading: Topping
items: Microwave the strawberries until thawed, chop or slice them, and sweeten to taste.
Fill each crepe with the cream cheese mixture, roll up, and spoon strawberries over the top.

tips: **Savory dinner crepes:** use 6 eggs and 1 1/2 tsp salt, skip the vanilla, and cut the sugar to 2–4 Tbsp

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Crush the cornflakes and mix them with the Parmesan and ranch mix in a shallow dish.
Dip each chicken breast in melted butter, then press it into the cornflake mixture to coat.
Arrange in the pan and bake uncovered for about 45 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
1 can Italian stewed tomatoes, chopped or blended
1 cup mafalda pasta, or any small bite-size pasta
In a large pot, brown the sausage.
Add the onion and carrots and cook 3 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Add the broth, tomatoes, and tomato sauce and bring to a boil.
Stir in the pasta and boil until tender.
Just before serving, stir in the spinach until wilted.
Top each bowl with Parmesan, provolone or mozzarella, and basil.
Beat the cream, pulverized peppermints, and powdered sugar until stiff peaks form.
Pipe or spoon small mounds onto parchment paper. Sprinkle with the crushed peppermints.
Freeze until firm, about 20 minutes, then transfer to a freezer bag.
Drop a mound into a mug of hot chocolate.

recipes.title: Pizza Hut Pizza Dough

items: Stir together the warm water, yeast, and sugar. Let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Add the flour, salt, and olive oil and knead until smooth.
Let rest 10 minutes. Coat the dough lightly with oil, cover tightly, and let rise about 2 hours, until doubled.
Use right away, or refrigerate. An overnight rest in the fridge gives the best flavor.
Shape, top as desired, and bake at 475°F for 12–16 minutes.

tips: **Stuffed crust:** lay string cheese around the edge of the dough, fold the dough up and over the cheese, and pinch to seal.
Brush the crust with garlic butter after baking.

recipes.title: Pasta Italiano

items: Mince the garlic and sauté it in the olive oil over medium heat for about a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and crushed red pepper. Simmer, stirring occasionally, for about 40 minutes.
Toss the sauce with the cooked penne. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in mozzarella just before serving.

tips: The red pepper is spicy. Julie found even 1/4 tsp plenty for her family, so start small.
Serve with a green vegetable and bread for a light dinner.

recipes.title: Caramel Apple Salad

items: Drain the pineapple, saving the juice. Refrigerate the pineapple.
In a saucepan, whisk the pineapple juice, flour, sugar, vinegar, and egg. Heat gently over low heat, stirring, until warm and slightly thickened.
Add the marshmallows and stir until melted. Stir in the pineapple.
Chop the apples. Fold the apples, pecans, Cool Whip, and caramels into the chilled mixture.

tips: Serve within 5–8 hours of adding the caramels; after that they start to melt into the salad.

recipes.title: Fondant (Cream Candy Centers)

steps.heading: Cook
items: In a heavy saucepan, combine the sugar, half-and-half, whipping cream, corn syrup, salt, and **1 Tbsp** of the butter.
Set over medium-high heat and stir constantly and quickly until it reaches a rolling boil that you can't stir down.
Turn the heat to medium and **stop stirring completely.** Cook to the soft-ball stage, 236°F.
To double-check, drop a spoonful into ice water, wait 5–10 seconds, and press it together under the water. If it forms a soft ball you can lift out, it's ready.
Remove from the heat and drop in the remaining 1 Tbsp butter. Don't stir it in; just let it melt on top.

steps.heading: Cool and work
items: Cover the pan and cool it quickly in a sink of ice water or in the freezer until it's room temperature or slightly warmer.
Pour it onto a cookie sheet or clean countertop. Using a stiff metal spatula or putty knife, keep scraping it inward into a pile and turning it over.
It will start out glossy. Keep working it until it suddenly loses its shine, thickens, and looks like dry frosting. That means it has "turned."
Perfect fondant is matte and still soft. If it's matte and firm, knead it in your hands like clay; if it softens, it's fine. If it crumbles, it was overcooked.

steps.heading: Finish
items: Divide the batch and knead in flavorings, food coloring, nuts, and so on.
Roll into small balls. Layer them in a dish between sheets of wax paper and freeze until you're ready to dip.
Melt chocolate in batches and dip the centers. Roll in nuts or coconut if you like.

tips: 12 oz chocolate covers about 80 small candies (one batch). Have extra chocolate on hand.
Frozen centers keep up to 3 months in an airtight container.
Fondant is temperamental. Don't double the recipe without researching first.

Add the eggs, oil, and milk and stir just until moistened.
Spray the waffle iron with cooking spray before the first waffle (and again if they start to stick). Cook according to your waffle iron's directions.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Pancakes

items: Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt together in a large bowl.
Separate the eggs. Whisk the egg whites into the buttermilk. Whisk the egg yolks into the melted butter, then combine the two mixtures.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir **just until combined**. A few small lumps are fine; overmixing makes tough pancakes.
Heat a griddle until a drop of water dances on the surface. Butter it lightly, then wipe it with a paper towel.
Scoop the batter with an ice cream scoop or measuring cup for even pancakes. Cook 2–3 minutes total, flipping once bubbles form on top.

tips: No buttermilk? Stir 2 Tbsp vinegar or lemon juice into 2 cups milk and let it sit a few minutes.
Regular milk instead of buttermilk works too, and some of the family prefer it.
Keep finished pancakes warm in a 170°F oven for up to about an hour.
Make your own pancake mix by combining the dry ingredients; it keeps about 3 months in an airtight container.
notes: The egg-separating technique is based on Alton Brown's pancake tips.

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a Bundt pan.
Put the 1/3 cup sugar and the cinnamon in a plastic bag. Add the biscuit pieces and shake to coat.
Layer the coated pieces in the pan and sprinkle any leftover cinnamon sugar over the top.
In a small saucepan, bring the 1/2 cup sugar, brown sugar, and butter to a boil. Pour it evenly over the biscuits.
Bake for about 30 minutes, until cooked through.
Let cool a few minutes, then gently turn out onto a serving plate.

recipes.title: Mom's Bread

items: In a large bowl, stir together the warm water, honey, yeast, and salt. Stir in the oil.
Add the flour and mix until a dough forms, then knead until smooth and elastic.
Let the dough rise in the bowl for 30 minutes.
Move it to a clean greased bowl and let it rise until doubled. Punch it down and let it rise until doubled again.
Divide the dough in half, shape into loaves, and place in 2 greased loaf pans. Let rise until puffy.
Turn the loaves out of the pans and brush the tops with butter.

tips: Use any mix of whole wheat and white flour you like.

recipes.title: Taco Chili

items: 1 can diced tomatoes with green chiles
Brown the ground beef in a large pot and drain the fat.
Add the taco seasoning, ranch mix, dried onion, chili powder, cumin, water, diced tomatoes with green chiles, tomato sauce, and beans.
Bring to a simmer and cook until heated through.
Serve with corn chips or tortilla chips.

tips: For more heat, use a hot taco seasoning mix.

recipes.title: Aunt Amy's Chili

items: Brown the ground beef in a large pot and drain off the fat.
Add the beans **with their liquid** (do not drain them), the tomatoes, cumin, chili powder, vinegar, and sugar.
Simmer for about 15 minutes, until heated through.
Serve with sour cream, green onions, cheese, avocado, and chips or crackers.

tips: Any combination of canned beans works.

Meanwhile, beat the eggs until they are thick and pale yellow.
Add the milk, flour, and salt and beat until smooth.
Pour the batter into the hot pan of melted butter.
Bake for 15–20 minutes, until puffed and golden. Serve right away with syrup.
